title.zh: 卷一百五十五 志第一百〇八 選舉一
title.en: Volume 155 Treatises 108: Selection and Appointment of Officials 1
title.raw: 卷一百五十五 志第一百〇八 選舉一 Volume 155 Treatises 108: Selection and Appointment of Officials 1

sentences.zh: 選舉一

translations.literal: Selection and Appointment 1
translations.idiomatic: Selection and Appointment, Part One

sentences.zh: 〈（科目上）〉

translations.literal: (Examination Categories, Part One)
translations.idiomatic: (Examination Categories, Part One)

sentences.zh: 自敷奏以言，明試以功，三載考績，三考黜陟幽明，始於《舜典》。

translations.literal: From presenting memorials to speak, to clearly testing by merit, to examining achievements over three years, and through three examinations promoting the worthy and demoting the unworthy—this began in the Canon of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: From memorials and spoken counsel, to testing merit in the open, to triennial review of performance, and through three rounds of examination distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy—all this began in the Canon of Shun.

sentences.zh: 司徒以鄉三物興賢能，太宰以三歲計吏治，詳於《周官》。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education raised the worthy and able through the three things of the district; the Grand Steward reckoned officials' governance every three years—the details are set forth in the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education promoted the worthy and able by the district's three standards; the Grand Steward assessed official performance every three years—as detailed in the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 兩漢而下，選舉之製不同，歸於得賢而已。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties onward, the systems of selection and appointment differed, yet all came down to obtaining the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasties onward, methods of selection and appointment varied, but all aimed at the same end: finding worthy men.

sentences.zh: 考其大要，不過入仕則有貢舉之科，服官則有銓選之格，任事則有考課之法。

translations.literal: Examining the main points, there were nothing more than categories for tribute-recommendation upon entering office, standards for selection and appointment upon taking posts, and methods for performance evaluation upon undertaking duties.
translations.idiomatic: In broad outline, entry to office rested on tribute and recommendation; appointment to posts on selection standards; and assessment of service on evaluation procedures.

sentences.zh: 然曆代之議貢舉者每曰：“取士以文藝，不若以德行。

translations.literal: Yet those who discussed tribute-recommendation in successive dynasties often said: "To select scholars by literary accomplishment is not as good as doing so by virtue and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yet critics of the tribute system in every age would say: "Selecting scholars by literary skill is inferior to selecting them by virtue and character.

sentences.zh: 就文藝而參酌之，賦論之浮華，不若經義之實學。”

translations.literal: Weighing literary accomplishment, the florid style of fu and discourse essays is not as good as the solid learning of classical interpretation."
translations.idiomatic: Even within literary tests, the ornate excess of rhapsodies and essays pales beside the substantive learning of classical interpretation."

sentences.zh: 議銓選者每曰：“以年勞取人，可以絕超躐，而不無賢愚同滯之歎；

translations.literal: Those who discussed selection and appointment often said: "Taking men by years of service can end leapfrogging promotions, yet it is not without the lament that the worthy and the foolish stagnate alike;
translations.idiomatic: Those who debated appointment standards often said: "Promoting by seniority can curb leapfrogging, yet it leaves the worthy and the mediocre stuck together alike;

sentences.zh: 以薦舉取人，可以拔俊傑，而不無巧佞捷進之弊。”

translations.literal: taking men by recommendation can raise outstanding talents, yet it is not without the abuse of the clever and sycophantic advancing swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: while recommendation can lift exceptional talent, it also opens the door to the clever and obsequious racing ahead."

sentences.zh: 議考課者每曰：“拘吏文，則上下督察，浸成澆風；

translations.literal: Those who discussed performance evaluation often said: "If bound by clerical paperwork, then superiors and subordinates supervise one another and gradually a corrupting custom takes shape;
translations.idiomatic: Critics of performance review said: "Tie officials to paperwork, and oversight from above and below breeds a culture of hollow compliance;

sentences.zh: 通譽望，則權貴請托，徒開利路。”

translations.literal: if reputation and standing prevail, then the powerful and noble seek favors, opening profit-seeking paths in vain."
translations.idiomatic: rely on reputation instead, and the powerful trade favors—opening nothing but avenues of private gain."

sentences.zh: 於是議論紛紜，莫之一也。

translations.literal: Thus discussions were tangled and none could be unified.
translations.idiomatic: And so debate swirled on, with no single settled view.

sentences.zh: 宋初承唐製，貢舉雖廣，而莫重於進士、製科，其次則三學選補。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, following Tang institutions, tribute-recommendation was broad, yet nothing weighed more heavily than the jinshi and special decree categories; next came selection and supplementation through the Three Academies.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song followed Tang practice: tribute examinations were many, but none mattered more than the jinshi and special decree categories, with selection through the Three Academies next in importance.

sentences.zh: 銓法雖多，而莫重於舉削改官、磨勘轉秩。

translations.literal: Selection methods were numerous, yet nothing weighed more heavily than memorial recommendations for rank changes and scrutinized reviews for promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Appointment rules were many, but none counted more than memorial recommendations for rank changes and scrutinized reviews for promotion.

sentences.zh: 考課雖密，而莫重於官給曆紙，驗考批書。

translations.literal: Performance evaluation was strict, yet nothing weighed more heavily than the calendar sheets issued by the office and the verification of evaluation endorsements.
translations.idiomatic: Performance review was rigorous, but its heart lay in the official calendar sheets and the signed endorsements that verified each assessment.

sentences.zh: 其他教官、武舉、童子等試，以及遺逸奏薦、貴戚公卿任子親屬與遠州流外諸選，委曲瑣細，咸有品式。

translations.literal: Other examinations—for teaching officials, military candidates, child prodigies, and the like—as well as memorial recommendations of recluses, appointment of sons and relatives of nobles and high ministers, and various selections in remote prefectures and outside the regular rolls—all had detailed, minute regulations and fixed forms.
translations.idiomatic: Other paths—exams for instructors, military candidates, and child prodigies; memorial recommendations of recluses; appointments for sons and kin of the nobility; selections in remote prefectures and outside the regular rolls—all had their own elaborate, fixed procedures.

sentences.zh: 其間變更不常，沿革迭見，而三百餘年元臣碩輔，鴻博之儒，清強之吏，皆自此出，得人為最盛焉。

translations.literal: Among these, changes were frequent and successive evolutions appeared, yet over more than three hundred years chief ministers and great aides, broadly learned scholars, and upright, capable officials all came from this system; in obtaining men it was at its most flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Rules changed often and reforms piled one upon another, yet for more than three centuries chief ministers, great scholars, and upright officials all emerged through this system—it produced talent on a scale unmatched.

sentences.zh: 今輯舊史所錄，臚為六門：一曰科目；

translations.literal: Now compiling what the old histories record, they are arranged in six categories: first, examination categories;
translations.idiomatic: Here we compile what the old histories record and arrange it in six sections: first, examination categories;

sentences.zh: 二曰學校試；

translations.literal: second, school examinations;
translations.idiomatic: second, school examinations;

sentences.zh: 三曰銓法；

translations.literal: third, selection methods;
translations.idiomatic: third, selection methods;

sentences.zh: 四曰補蔭；

translations.literal: fourth, yin privilege appointments;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, yin privilege appointments;

sentences.zh: 五曰保任；

translations.literal: fifth, guarantor appointment;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, guarantor appointment;

sentences.zh: 六曰考課。

translations.literal: sixth, performance evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, performance evaluation.

sentences.zh: 煩簡適中，隱括歸類，作《選舉志》。

translations.literal: Choosing what is detailed or concise in due measure and gathering it into categories, the Treatise on Selection and Appointment was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Selecting what is essential without excess and grouping it by category, we compose the Treatise on Selection and Appointment.

sentences.zh: 宋之科目，有進士，有諸科，有武舉。

translations.literal: Song examination categories included jinshi, various specialized categories, and military examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Song examination categories included the jinshi, various specialized subjects, and military examinations.

sentences.zh: 常選之外，又有制科，有童子舉，而進士得人為盛。

translations.literal: Beyond the regular selections there were also special decree categories and child prodigy examinations, yet jinshi produced talent most abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the regular examinations were special decree categories and child prodigy tests, but the jinshi track yielded talent in the greatest abundance.

sentences.zh: 神宗始罷諸科，而分經義、詩賦以取士，其後遵行，未之有改。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong first abolished the various specialized categories and divided selection between classical interpretation and poetry-rhapsody; thereafter this was followed and never changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong first abolished the specialized categories and split selection between classical interpretation and poetry-rhapsody—a division that thereafter remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 自仁宗命郡縣建學，而熙寧以來，其法浸備，學校之設遍天下，而海內文治彬彬矣。

translations.literal: From the time Emperor Renzong ordered prefectures and counties to establish schools, and from the Xining era onward, the regulations gradually became complete; schools were established throughout the realm, and cultural governance within the Four Seas was flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Renzong's order that every prefecture and county establish schools, and especially from the Xining reforms onward, the system grew ever more complete—schools spread across the realm, and cultural order flourished throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 今以科目、學校之製，各著於篇。

translations.literal: Now the institutions of examination categories and schools are each set forth in their sections.
translations.idiomatic: The institutions governing examination categories and schools are each treated in their own sections below.

sentences.zh: 初，禮部貢舉，設進士、《九經》、《五經》、《開元禮》、《三史》、《三禮》、《三傳》、學究、明經、明法等科，皆秋取解，冬集禮部，春考試。

translations.literal: At first, the Ministry of Rites tribute-recommendation established categories of jinshi, Nine Classics, Five Classics, Kaiyuan Rites, Three Histories, Three Rites, Three Commentaries, Classicist, Classics Understanding, and Law Understanding—all took qualifying exams in autumn, assembled at the Ministry of Rites in winter, and were examined in spring.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Ministry of Rites set up jinshi and specialized categories—the Nine Classics, Five Classics, Kaiyuan Rites, Three Histories, Three Rites, Three Commentaries, Classicist, Classics Understanding, and Law Understanding. Candidates submitted qualifying exams in autumn, assembled at the Ministry in winter, and sat the final examination in spring.

sentences.zh: 合格及第者，列名放榜於尚書省。

translations.literal: Those who passed and received degrees had their names listed and the results posted at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed were listed by name and the results posted at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡進士，試詩、賦、論各一首，策五道，帖《論語》十帖，對《春秋》或《禮記》墨義十條。

translations.literal: For jinshi, one each of poetry, rhapsody, and discourse essay were tested, five policy questions, ten fill-in passages from the Analects, and ten written classical interpretations on the Spring and Autumn Annals or Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi candidates were tested on one poem, one rhapsody, and one essay; five policy questions; ten fill-in passages from the Analects; and ten written classical interpretations on either the Spring and Autumn Annals or the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡《九經》，帖書一百二十帖，對墨義六十條。

translations.literal: For the Nine Classics, one hundred twenty fill-in passages and sixty written classical interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: For the Nine Classics track: one hundred twenty fill-in passages and sixty written classical interpretations.

sentences.zh: 凡《五經》，帖書八十帖，對墨義五十條。

translations.literal: For the Five Classics, eighty fill-in passages and fifty written classical interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: For the Five Classics track: eighty fill-in passages and fifty written classical interpretations.

sentences.zh: 凡《三禮》，對墨義九十條。

translations.literal: For the Three Rites, ninety written classical interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: For the Three Rites track: ninety written classical interpretations.

sentences.zh: 凡《三傳》，一百一十條，凡《開元禮》，凡《三史》，各對三百條。

translations.literal: For the Three Commentaries, one hundred ten items; for the Kaiyuan Rites and Three Histories, each three hundred written interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: For the Three Commentaries: one hundred ten items. For the Kaiyuan Rites and Three Histories: three hundred written interpretations each.

sentences.zh: 凡學究，《毛詩》對墨義五十條，《論語》十條，《爾雅》、《孝經》共十條，《周易》、《尚書》各二十五條。

translations.literal: For Classicist, fifty written interpretations on the Mao Odes, ten on the Analects, ten combined on the Erya and Classic of Filial Piety, and twenty-five each on the Book of Changes and Book of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Classicist candidates faced fifty written interpretations on the Mao Odes, ten on the Analects, ten combined on the Erya and Classic of Filial Piety, and twenty-five each on the Book of Changes and Book of Documents.

sentences.zh: 凡明法，對律令四十條，兼經並同《毛詩》之製。

translations.literal: For Law Understanding, forty written responses on statutes and ordinances; the supplementary classics followed the same format as the Mao Odes category.
translations.idiomatic: Law Understanding candidates answered forty questions on statutes and ordinances; supplementary classic requirements followed the Mao Odes format.

sentences.zh: 各間經引試，通六為合格，仍抽卷問律，本科則否。

translations.literal: Each was tested at intervals with classical citations; passing six out of ten qualified, and law was still tested by random roll check, but not for the main category.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates were tested at intervals with classical citations; six correct answers qualified. Law was also tested by random roll check, except for the main law category itself.

sentences.zh: 諸州判官試進士，錄事參軍試諸科，不通經義，則別選官考校，而判官監之。

translations.literal: Prefectural judges examined jinshi candidates; recording secretaries examined other categories. If they did not understand classical interpretation, separate officials were chosen to grade the exams while the judge supervised.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural judges examined jinshi candidates and recording secretaries examined other categories. If examiners lacked classical training, other officials were appointed to grade the papers under judicial supervision.

sentences.zh: 試紙，長官印署面給之。

translations.literal: Examination papers were sealed with the chief official's stamp on the face and then issued.
translations.idiomatic: Examination papers were stamped on the cover by the chief official before being issued.

sentences.zh: 試中格者，第其甲乙，具所試經義，朱書通、否，監官、試官署名其下。

translations.literal: Those who passed were ranked in order of merit; the classical interpretations tested were listed, pass or fail written in red, and the supervising and examining officials signed below.
translations.idiomatic: Successful candidates were ranked in order; their classical interpretations were recorded with pass or fail marked in red, and supervising and examining officials signed below.

sentences.zh: 進士文卷，諸科義卷、帖由，並隨解牒上之禮部。

translations.literal: Jinshi literary papers, specialized-category interpretation papers, and fill-in receipts were all sent up to the Ministry of Rites with the qualifying documents.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi papers, specialized-category interpretation sheets, and fill-in receipts were all forwarded to the Ministry of Rites with the qualifying documents.

sentences.zh: 有篤廢疾者不得貢。

translations.literal: Those with serious chronic illness were not permitted to be recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates with serious chronic illness were barred from recommendation.

sentences.zh: 貢不應法及校試不以實者，監官、試官停任。

translations.literal: If recommendations did not conform to regulations or grading was not truthful, supervising and examining officials were suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: If recommendations violated regulations or grading was falsified, supervising and examining officials were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 受賂，則論以枉法，長官奏裁。

translations.literal: If bribes were accepted, they were prosecuted for perversion of law, and the chief official memorialized for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting bribes was prosecuted as perversion of law, with the chief official memorializing for imperial judgment.

sentences.zh: 凡命士應舉，謂之鎖廳試。

translations.literal: For commissioned scholars taking examinations, this was called the locked-hall examination.
translations.idiomatic: When commissioned scholars sat the examinations, it was called the locked-hall examination.

sentences.zh: 所屬先以名聞，得旨而後解。

translations.literal: Their department first reported their names; only after receiving imperial approval could they submit qualifying documents.
translations.idiomatic: Their department first submitted their names and could send qualifying documents only after receiving imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 既集，什伍相保，不許有大逆人緦麻以上親，及諸不孝、不悌、隱匿工商異類、僧道歸俗之徒。

translations.literal: Once assembled, they were grouped in fives and tens as mutual guarantors; those with relatives within mourning for great treason, and various unfilial, undutiful, or hidden artisan-merchant outcast persons, or monks and Daoists who had returned to lay life, were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once assembled, candidates formed mutual-guarantee groups of five and ten. Excluded were relatives within mourning for great treason, the unfilial and undutiful, those concealing artisan or merchant status, and monks or Daoists who had returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 家狀並試卷之首，署年及舉數、場第、鄉貫，不得增損移易，以仲冬收納，月終而畢。

translations.literal: On household registers and at the head of examination papers were recorded age, number of attempts, session rank, and native place; these could not be added to, reduced, or altered. Collection was in mid-winter and completed by month's end.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers and exam cover sheets recorded age, number of attempts, session rank, and native place—none of which could be altered. Papers were collected in mid-winter and due by month's end.

sentences.zh: 將臨試期，知舉官先引問聯保，與狀僉同而定焉。

translations.literal: As the examination period approached, the chief examiner first summoned and questioned the mutual guarantors and confirmed agreement with the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Before the examination, the chief examiner summoned mutual guarantors for questioning and verified their records against the registers.

sentences.zh: 凡就試，唯詞賦者許持《切韻》、《玉篇》，其挾書為奸，及口相受授者，發覺即黜之。

translations.literal: For those taking the examination, only candidates in poetry and rhapsody were permitted to carry the Qieyun and Yupian; those who brought forbidden books to cheat, or who orally transmitted answers, were dismissed upon discovery.
translations.idiomatic: Only poetry and rhapsody candidates could bring the Qieyun and Yupian. Cheating with hidden texts or oral collusion meant immediate dismissal.

sentences.zh: 凡諸州長吏舉送，必先稽其版藉，察其行為；

translations.literal: For all prefectural chiefs recommending candidates, they first had to check household registers and investigate conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural chiefs recommending candidates first verified household registers and investigated conduct;

sentences.zh: 鄉里所推，每十人相保，內有缺行，則連坐不得舉。

translations.literal: those recommended by the community were grouped in tens as mutual guarantors; if any within the group had deficient conduct, all were punished by association and could not be recommended.
translations.idiomatic: community nominees formed groups of ten as mutual guarantors; if any member's conduct was deficient, the whole group was barred from recommendation.

sentences.zh: 故事，知舉官將赴貢院，台閣近臣得薦所知之負藝者，號曰“公薦”。

translations.literal: By precedent, when the chief examiner was about to enter the examination compound, close ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery could recommend talented persons they knew, called "public recommendation."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, as the chief examiner entered the examination compound, close ministers could recommend talented acquaintances—called "public recommendation."

sentences.zh: 太祖慮其因緣挾私，禁之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu, fearing private connections and favoritism, forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu, fearing nepotism and private favor, banned the practice.

sentences.zh: 自唐以來，所謂明經，不過帖書、墨義，觀其記誦而已，故賤其科，而“不通”者其罰特重。

translations.literal: From Tang times, so-called Classics Understanding amounted only to fill-in passages and written classical interpretations, testing memorization alone; therefore the category was held cheap, and the penalty for "failure" was especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang times, Classics Understanding tested little beyond fill-in passages and rote interpretation—memorization, not understanding—so the category was despised and failure carried especially harsh penalties.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，詔曰：“舊制，《九經》一舉不第而止，非所以啟迪仕進之路也；

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, an edict said: "Under the old system, failure in the Nine Classics after one attempt ended further tries—this is not how to open the path of office and advancement;
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 1, an edict declared: "Under the old rule, one failure in the Nine Classics ended a candidate's career—that is no way to keep the path to office open;

sentences.zh: 自今依諸科許再試。”

translations.literal: from now on, as with other categories, a second attempt is permitted."
translations.idiomatic: hereafter, as with other categories, candidates may try again."

sentences.zh: 是年，諸州所薦士數益多，乃約周顯德之製，定諸州貢舉條法及殿罰之式：進士“文理紕繆”者殿五舉，諸科初場十“不”殿五舉，第二、第三場十“不”殿三舉，第一至第三場九“不”並殿一舉。

translations.literal: That year, as recommended scholars from the prefectures grew ever more numerous, regulations based on the Zhou Xiande system were set for prefectural tribute-recommendation and penalties for failing sessions: jinshi with "confused reasoning and wording" were barred for five sessions; in other categories, ten "failures" in the first session barred five sessions, ten "failures" in the second or third barred three sessions, and nine "failures" across all three sessions barred one session.
translations.idiomatic: That year, with prefectural recommendations swelling, rules modeled on Zhou Xiande set tribute procedures and failure penalties: jinshi with "confused reasoning" were barred five sessions; specialized categories faced graduated penalties for accumulated failures across sessions.

sentences.zh: 殿舉之數，朱書於試卷，送中書門下。

translations.literal: The number of barred sessions was written in red on the examination paper and sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Barred-session counts were marked in red on examination papers and sent to the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 三年，陶穀子邴擢上第，帝曰：“穀不能訓子，安得登第？”

translations.literal: In the third year, Tao Gu's son Bing was selected for top rank. The emperor said: "Gu could not instruct his son—how could he pass the examination?"
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Tao Gu's son Bing ranked first. The emperor said: "Gu could not teach his own son—how did he pass?"

sentences.zh: 乃詔：“食祿之家，有登第者，禮部具姓名以聞，令覆試之。”

translations.literal: An edict then ordered: "For salary-receiving families with degree holders, the Ministry of Rites shall list names and report; they shall be re-examined."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "When salary-receiving families produced degree holders, the Ministry of Rites must report their names for re-examination."

sentences.zh: 自是，別命儒臣於中書覆試，合格乃賜第。

translations.literal: From this time, Confucian officials were separately appointed at the Secretariat for re-examination; only after passing were degrees granted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Confucian officials at the Secretariat re-examined such candidates; degrees were granted only after they passed.

sentences.zh: 時川蜀、荊湖內附，試數道所貢士，縣次往還續食。

translations.literal: At the time Sichuan, Huguang, and other newly submitted regions sent recommended scholars; travel rations were provided for round trips by county order.
translations.idiomatic: As Sichuan, Huguang, and other newly submitted regions sent candidates, counties provided travel rations for the round trip.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，詔禮部閱貢士及十五舉嚐終場者，得一百六人，賜本科出身。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to review recommended scholars who had attempted fifteen times and completed every session; one hundred six persons were found and granted degrees in their respective categories.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 3, the Ministry of Rites reviewed candidates who had attempted fifteen times and always completed the full examination; one hundred six were granted degrees in their categories.

sentences.zh: 特奏名恩例，蓋自此始。

translations.literal: The special memorial-name favor, it may be said, began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The special memorial-name privilege began at this point.

sentences.zh: 五年，禮部奏合格進士、諸科凡二十八人，上親召對講武殿，而未及引試也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Ministry of Rites reported twenty-eight qualified jinshi and specialized-category candidates; the emperor personally summoned them for audience at the Lecture on Military Affairs Hall, though the oral examination had not yet been held.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the Ministry reported twenty-eight qualified jinshi and specialized candidates; the emperor summoned them to the Lecture on Military Affairs Hall, though oral examination had not yet taken place.

sentences.zh: 明年，翰林學士李昉知貢舉，取宋準以下十一人，而進士武濟川、《三傳》劉睿材質最陋，對問失次，上黜之。

translations.literal: The following year, Hanlin Academician Li Fang served as chief examiner and selected eleven persons including Song Zhun; but jinshi Wu Jichuan and Three Commentaries Liu Rui had the coarsest quality and answered out of order in oral questioning, and the emperor dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Hanlin Academician Li Fang served as chief examiner and selected eleven candidates including Song Zhun—but jinshi Wu Jichuan and Three Commentaries candidate Liu Rui were the weakest; they fumbled the oral examination and were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 濟川，昉鄉人也。

translations.literal: Jichuan was a fellow townsman of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Jichuan was from Fang's home district.

sentences.zh: 會有訴昉用情取舍，帝乃籍終場下第人姓名，得三百六十人，皆召見，擇其一百九十五人，並準以下，乃禦殿給紙筆，別試詩賦。

translations.literal: When there were complaints that Fang had shown favor in selection, the emperor registered the names of those who completed the session but failed, finding three hundred sixty persons; all were summoned for audience, and one hundred ninety-five were chosen together with Zhun and those below him; then paper and brush were provided in the imperial hall for a separate poetry and rhapsody examination.
translations.idiomatic: When complaints arose that Fang had favored certain candidates, the emperor registered everyone who had completed the examination but failed—three hundred sixty in all. He summoned them, selected one hundred ninety-five together with Zhun and those ranked below him, and held a separate poetry and rhapsody examination in the imperial hall.

sentences.zh: 命殿中侍御史李瑩等為考官，得進士二十六人，《五經》四人，《開元禮》七人，《三禮》三十八人，《三傳》二十六人，《三史》三人，學究十八人，明法五人，皆賜及第，又賜錢二十萬以張宴會。

translations.literal: Palace Diarist Li Ying and others were appointed examiners; twenty-six jinshi, four Five Classics, seven Kaiyuan Rites, thirty-eight Three Rites, twenty-six Three Commentaries, three Three Histories, eighteen Classicist, and five Law Understanding candidates were obtained—all granted degrees, and two hundred thousand cash was bestowed to expand the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Diarist Li Ying and others served as examiners. Twenty-six jinshi plus candidates in Five Classics, Kaiyuan Rites, Three Rites, Three Commentaries, Three Histories, Classicist, and Law Understanding—all received degrees. Two hundred thousand cash was granted to expand the celebration banquet.

sentences.zh: 昉等尋皆坐責。

translations.literal: Fang and the others soon all suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his colleagues were soon all punished.

sentences.zh: 殿試遂為常製。

translations.literal: The palace examination thus became a regular institution.
translations.idiomatic: The palace examination thus became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 帝嚐語近臣曰：“昔者，科名多為勢家所取，朕親臨試，盡革其弊矣。”

translations.literal: The emperor once told close ministers: "In former times, examination honors were mostly taken by powerful families; I personally preside over the examination and have completely reformed these abuses."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told close ministers: "In the past, examination honors went mostly to powerful families. By presiding personally, I have swept those abuses away."

sentences.zh: 八年，親試進士王式等，乃定王嗣宗第一，王式第四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he personally examined jinshi including Wang Shi and set Wang Sigong first and Wang Shi fourth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he personally examined jinshi including Wang Shi, ranking Wang Sigong first and Wang Shi fourth.

sentences.zh: 自是禦試與省試名次，始有升降之別。

translations.literal: From this time the rankings of the palace examination and the provincial examination began to have differences of promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, palace examination rankings could differ from provincial examination rankings—promotions and demotions between the two became possible.

sentences.zh: 時江南未平，進士林鬆、雷說試不中格，以其間道來歸，亦賜《三傳》出身。

translations.literal: At the time the Jiangnan region was not yet pacified; jinshi Lin Song and Lei Shuo failed to qualify but came over by secret route and were also granted Three Commentaries degrees.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiangnan remained unconquered, jinshi candidates Lin Song and Lei Shuo had failed the examination but defected through secret routes; they too were granted Three Commentaries degrees.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，思振淹滯，謂侍臣曰：“朕欲博求俊彥於科場中，非敢望拔十得五，止得一二，亦可為致治之具矣。”

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, thinking to revive those long stalled in office, he told attending ministers: "I wish to seek broadly for outstanding talents in the examination halls. I dare not hope to select five from ten—if I obtain one or two, that will suffice as instruments for bringing order."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, seeking to lift those long stalled in office, he told his ministers: "I mean to seek outstanding talent in the examination halls. I do not expect to find five in ten—even one or two will serve as instruments of good governance."

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，禦殿覆試，內出賦題，賦韻平側相間，依次而用。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, a palace re-examination was held; rhapsody topics were issued from within, with rhyme tones alternating level and oblique in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2, a palace re-examination was held. Rhapsody topics were issued from within the palace, with rhyme tones alternating level and oblique in order.

sentences.zh: 命李昉、扈蒙第其優劣為三等，得呂蒙正以下一百九人。

translations.literal: Li Fang and Hu Meng were ordered to rank excellence and inferiority in three grades, obtaining one hundred nine persons including Lü Mengzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang and Hu Meng ranked candidates in three grades, selecting one hundred nine including Lü Mengzheng.

sentences.zh: 越二日，覆試諸科，得二百人。

translations.literal: Two days later, specialized categories were re-examined, yielding two hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later specialized categories were re-examined, yielding two hundred candidates.

sentences.zh: 並賜及第。

translations.literal: All were granted degrees.
translations.idiomatic: All received degrees.

sentences.zh: 又閱貢藉，得十舉以上至十五舉進士、諸科一百八十餘人，並賜出身；

translations.literal: The tribute registers were also reviewed, finding more than one hundred eighty jinshi and specialized-category candidates with ten to fifteen attempts; all were granted degrees;
translations.idiomatic: Tribute registers were also reviewed, finding over one hundred eighty jinshi and specialized candidates with ten to fifteen attempts—all granted degrees;

sentences.zh: 《九經》七人不中格，亦憐其老，特賜同《三傳》出身。

translations.literal: seven Nine Classics candidates who failed were also pitied for their age and specially granted degrees equivalent to Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Seven failing Nine Classics candidates, pitied for their age, were specially granted degrees equivalent to Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 凡五百餘人，皆賜袍笏，錫宴開寶寺，帝自為詩二章賜之。

translations.literal: In all more than five hundred persons were granted robes and court tablets, feasted at Kaibao Temple, and the emperor personally composed two poems to bestow upon them.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred received robes and court tablets, were feasted at Kaibao Temple, and received two poems composed by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 甲、乙第進士及《九經》，皆授將作監丞、大理評事，通判諸州，其餘亦優等授官。

translations.literal: First- and second-rank jinshi and Nine Classics candidates were all appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Works and Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, serving as prefectural vice commissioners; the rest also received preferential appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Top-ranked jinshi and Nine Classics candidates were appointed Assistant Director of the Directorate of Works and Case Reviewer, serving as prefectural vice commissioners; others also received preferential appointments.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，廷試舉人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, a court examination of candidates was held.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year, a court examination was held.

sentences.zh: 故事，惟春放榜，至是秋試，非常例也。

translations.literal: By precedent, results were posted only in spring; this autumn examination was an extraordinary case.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent results were posted only in spring—this autumn examination was exceptional.

sentences.zh: 是冬，諸州舉人並集，會將親征北漢，罷之。

translations.literal: That winter, candidates from all prefectures had assembled, but as the emperor was about to campaign personally against Northern Han, it was cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter candidates from all prefectures had assembled, but with the emperor about to campaign against Northern Han, the examination was cancelled.

sentences.zh: 自是，間一年或二年乃貢舉。

translations.literal: From this time, tribute-recommendation was held every one or two years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute examinations were held every one or two years.

sentences.zh: 五年，覆試進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, jinshi were re-examined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year jinshi were re-examined.

sentences.zh: 有顏明遠、劉昌言、張觀、樂史四人，以見任官舉進士，特授近藩掌書記。

translations.literal: Yan Mingyuan, Liu Changyan, Zhang Guan, and Yue Shi—four persons who took the jinshi examination while holding office—were specially appointed secretaries in nearby fan administrations.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mingyuan, Liu Changyan, Zhang Guan, and Yue Shi—four incumbent officials who sat the jinshi examination—were specially appointed secretaries in nearby fan administrations.

sentences.zh: 有趙昌國者，求應百篇舉，謂一日作詩百篇。

translations.literal: One Zhao Changguo sought to take the Hundred-Poem examination, claiming he could compose one hundred poems in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Changguo sought the Hundred-Poem examination, claiming he could compose one hundred poems in a single day.

sentences.zh: 帝出雜題二十，令各賦五篇，篇八句。

translations.literal: The emperor issued twenty miscellaneous topics and ordered five poems on each, eight lines per poem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued twenty miscellaneous topics and required five poems on each, eight lines per poem.

sentences.zh: 日旰，僅成數十首，率無可觀。

translations.literal: By day's end he had completed only several dozen poems, generally unremarkable.
translations.idiomatic: By day's end he had completed only several dozen poems, none of much merit.

sentences.zh: 帝以是科久廢，特賜及第，以勸來者。

translations.literal: The emperor, because this category had long been abandoned, specially granted a degree to encourage future candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Because this category had long been discontinued, the emperor specially granted a degree to encourage others.

sentences.zh: 八年，進士、諸科始試律義十道，進士免帖經。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, jinshi and specialized categories first tested ten law-interpretation questions; jinshi were exempted from fill-in classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year jinshi and specialized categories first tested ten law-interpretation questions; jinshi were exempted from fill-in classics.

sentences.zh: 明年，惟諸科試律，進士復帖經。

translations.literal: The following year, only specialized categories tested law; jinshi again took fill-in classics.
translations.idiomatic: The next year only specialized categories tested law; jinshi again took fill-in classics.

sentences.zh: 進士始分三甲。

translations.literal: Jinshi were first divided into three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi were first divided into three ranks.

sentences.zh: 自是錫宴就瓊林苑。

translations.literal: From this time the grant banquet was held at the Qionglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the grant banquet was held at the Qionglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 上因謂近臣曰：“朕親選多士，殆忘饑渴，召見臨問，觀其才技而用之，庶使田野無遺逸，而朝廷多君子爾。”

translations.literal: The emperor therefore told close ministers: "I personally select many scholars, nearly forgetting hunger and thirst; I summon them for audience and questioning, observe their talents and employ them—perhaps thus the countryside will have no overlooked recluses and the court many gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told close ministers: "In selecting scholars I nearly forget hunger and thirst—I summon them, question them, observe their talents, and employ them—so that no talent in the countryside goes overlooked and the court may have true gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，廷試初唱名及第，第一等為節度推官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, at the court examination the names of those who received degrees were first announced; first-rank candidates were appointed as military commissioner staff evaluators.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2, degree recipients' names were first announced at the court examination; first-rank candidates were appointed military commissioner staff evaluators.

sentences.zh: 是年及端拱初，禮部試已，帝慮有遺才，取不中格者再試之，於是由再試得官者數百人。

translations.literal: That year and at the beginning of Duangong, after the Ministry of Rites examination was complete, the emperor feared overlooked talent and re-examined those who failed; thereby several hundred obtained office through re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: That year and at the start of Duangong, fearing overlooked talent after the Ministry examination, the emperor re-examined failures—several hundred gained office thereby.

sentences.zh: 凡廷試，帝親閱卷累日，宰相屢請宜歸有司，始詔歲命官知舉。

translations.literal: For court examinations, the emperor personally reviewed papers for many days; the chief councillors repeatedly requested that this be returned to the proper offices, and only then was it decreed that each year officials would be appointed as chief examiners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally reviewed examination papers for days; only after repeated requests from chief councillors was it decreed that officials would serve as chief examiners each year.

sentences.zh: 舊制，既鎖院，給左藏錢十萬資費用。

translations.literal: Under the old system, once the compound was locked, one hundred thousand cash from the Left Treasury was provided for expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, once the examination compound was locked, one hundred thousand cash from the Left Treasury covered expenses.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，詔改支尚書祠部，仍倍其數，罷禦廚、儀鸞司供帳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong, an edict changed payment to the Ministry of Rites Ancestral Temples Bureau, doubled the amount, and abolished provisions from the Imperial Kitchen and Ceremonial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 1, payment was shifted to the Ministry's Ancestral Temples Bureau at double the amount, abolishing Imperial Kitchen and Ceremonial Guard provisions.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉宋白等定貢院故事：先期三日，進士具都榜引試，借御史台驅使官一人監門，都堂簾外置案，設銀香爐，唱名給印試紙。

translations.literal: Chief examiners Song Bai and others established examination compound precedents: three days beforehand jinshi assembled for preliminary examination; an envoy of the Censorate was borrowed to guard the gate; outside the hall curtain a desk was placed with a silver incense burner; names were called and stamped examination papers issued.
translations.idiomatic: Chief examiners Song Bai and others established compound precedents: three days before, jinshi assembled for preliminary testing; a Censorate envoy guarded the gate; names were called and stamped papers issued outside the hall curtain.

sentences.zh: 及試中格，錄進士之文奏禦，諸科惟籍名而上；

translations.literal: When candidates passed, jinshi papers were submitted to the emperor; specialized categories only listed names;
translations.idiomatic: Successful jinshi papers were submitted to the emperor; specialized categories only listed names;

sentences.zh: 俟製下，先書姓名散報之，翌日，放傍唱名。

translations.literal: after the decree was issued, names were first written out and distributed; the next day results were posted and names announced.
translations.idiomatic: after the decree, names were distributed first; results were posted and announced the next day.

sentences.zh: 既謝恩，詣國學謁先聖先師，進士過堂閤下告名。

translations.literal: After expressing thanks, they visited the Imperial Academy to pay respects to the sage and his teacher; jinshi reported their names below the Hall Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After the thanksgiving audience they visited the Imperial Academy to honor the sage and his teacher; jinshi reported their names at the Hall Gate.

sentences.zh: 聞喜宴分為兩日，宴進士，請丞郎、大兩省；

translations.literal: The Joyous Announcement Banquet was divided over two days: jinshi were feasted, with vice directors and grand secretaries invited;
translations.idiomatic: The Joyous Announcement Banquet spanned two days: jinshi were feasted with vice directors and grand secretaries invited;

sentences.zh: 宴諸科，請省郎、小兩省。

translations.literal: specialized categories were feasted, with bureau directors and junior grand secretaries invited.
translations.idiomatic: specialized categories were feasted with bureau directors and junior grand secretaries invited.

sentences.zh: 綴行期集，列敘名氏、鄉貫、三代之類書之，謂之小錄。

translations.literal: A procession schedule was compiled listing names, native places, and three generations of ancestry—a booklet called the small register.
translations.idiomatic: A procession schedule listed names, native places, and three generations—the small register.

sentences.zh: 醵錢為遊宴之資，謂之酺。

translations.literal: Funds were pooled for touring banquets—called the contribution feast.
translations.idiomatic: Funds were pooled for touring banquets—the contribution feast.

sentences.zh: 皆團司主之。

translations.literal: All were managed by the group officers.
translations.idiomatic: Group officers managed all of this.

sentences.zh: 製下，而中書省同貢院關黃覆奏之，俟正敕下，關報南曹、都省、御史台，然後貢院寫春關散給。

translations.literal: When the decree was issued, the Secretariat and examination compound jointly submitted a yellow memorial for review; after the formal decree arrived, notification was sent to the Southern Bureau, Department of State Affairs, and Censorate; then the examination compound copied the spring gate notice for distribution.
translations.idiomatic: When the decree issued, the Secretariat and compound submitted a yellow memorial for review; after the formal decree, the Southern Bureau, Department of State Affairs, and Censorate were notified; then the compound distributed the spring gate notice.

sentences.zh: 〈（籍而入選謂之春關。）〉

translations.literal: (Those registered and entering selection were called the spring gate.)
translations.idiomatic: (Those registered and entering selection were called the spring gate.)

sentences.zh: 登科之人，例納朱膠綾紙之直，赴吏部南曹試判三道，謂之關試。

translations.literal: Degree recipients customarily paid the cost of vermilion glue and silk paper, went to the Ministry of Personnel Southern Bureau to test on three judgment cases—called the gate examination.
translations.idiomatic: Degree recipients customarily paid for vermilion glue and silk paper, then tested on three judgment cases at the Ministry's Southern Bureau—the gate examination.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，諸道貢士凡萬七千餘人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, recommended scholars from all circuits totaled more than seventeen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3, recommended scholars from all circuits exceeded seventeen thousand.

sentences.zh: 先是，有擊登聞鼓訴校試不公者。

translations.literal: Previously, some had struck the petition drum complaining of unfair grading.
translations.idiomatic: Previously some had struck the petition drum protesting unfair grading.

sentences.zh: 蘇易簡知貢舉，受詔即赴貢院，仍糊名考校，遂為例。

translations.literal: Su Yijian served as chief examiner; receiving the decree he went directly to the examination compound, still sealed names for grading—this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian, as chief examiner, went directly to the compound upon receiving the decree and sealed names for grading—establishing precedent.

sentences.zh: 既廷試，帝諭多士曰：“爾等各負誌業，效官之外，更勵精文采，無墜前功也。”

translations.literal: After the court examination, the emperor addressed the scholars: "Each of you bears his own ambition and learning; beyond serving in office, further refine your literary talent and do not fall from former achievement."
translations.idiomatic: After the court examination the emperor told the scholars: "Each of you has his own ambition and learning; beyond office, refine your literary talent and do not fall from what you have achieved."

sentences.zh: 詔刻《禮記·儒行篇》賜之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Confucian Conduct chapter of the Record of Rites carved and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Confucian Conduct chapter of the Record of Rites carved and distributed.

sentences.zh: 每科進士第一人，天子寵之以詩，後嚐作箴賜陳堯叟，至是，並賜焉。

translations.literal: Each session's top jinshi was honored by the Son of Heaven with a poem; later an admonition was also bestowed on Chen Yaosou, and from this time both were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Each session's top jinshi received an imperial poem; later an admonition was also bestowed on Chen Yaosou, and thereafter both were granted.

sentences.zh: 先是，嚐並學究、《尚書》、《周易》為一科，始更定本經日試義十道，《尚書》、《周易》各義五道，仍雜問疏義六道，經注四道。

translations.literal: Previously, Classicist, Book of Documents, and Book of Changes had been combined into one category; now the original classic was fixed with ten daily interpretation questions—five each on Documents and Changes—plus six mixed commentary questions and four classic-gloss questions.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Classicist, Documents, and Changes had been one category; now each original classic required ten daily interpretation questions—five each on Documents and Changes—plus six commentary and four gloss questions.

sentences.zh: 明法舊試六場，更定試七場：第一、第二場試律，第三場試令，第四、第五場試小經，第六場試令，第七場試律，仍於試律日雜問疏義六、經注四。

translations.literal: Law Understanding had tested six sessions; now seven were fixed: first and second sessions law, third statutes, fourth and fifth minor classics, sixth statutes, seventh law, with six mixed commentary and four gloss questions on the law session.
translations.idiomatic: Law Understanding expanded from six to seven sessions: law, law, statutes, minor classics, minor classics, statutes, law—with six commentary and four gloss questions on the law day.

sentences.zh: 凡《三禮》、《三傳》、《通禮》每十道義分經注六道、疏義四道，以六通為合格。

translations.literal: For Three Rites, Three Commentaries, and Comprehensive Rites, every ten interpretation questions divided six classic-gloss and four commentary questions; six correct qualified.
translations.idiomatic: For Three Rites, Three Commentaries, and Comprehensive Rites, ten questions apportioned six gloss and four commentary; six correct answers qualified.

sentences.zh: 自淳化末，停貢舉五年。

translations.literal: From the end of Chunhua, tribute-recommendation was suspended for five years.
translations.idiomatic: From the end of Chunhua, tribute examinations were suspended five years.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，復試，而高句麗始貢一人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, examinations resumed, and Goryeo first sent one candidate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne examinations resumed, and Goryeo first sent one candidate.

sentences.zh: 先是，國子監、開封府所貢士，與舉送官為姻戚，則兩司更互考試，始命遣官別試。

translations.literal: Previously, scholars submitted by the Directorate of Education and Kaifeng Prefecture who were related by marriage to recommending officials were examined alternately by the two offices; now officials were specially dispatched for separate examination.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Directorate and Kaifeng candidates related by marriage to recommenders were examined alternately; now separate examiners were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，親試陳堯谘等八百四十人，特奏名者九百餘人，有晉天福中嚐預貢者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, Chen Yaozi and eight hundred forty others were personally examined; more than nine hundred special memorial-name candidates included some who had submitted in the Jin Tianfu era.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, Chen Yaozi and eight hundred forty others were personally examined; over nine hundred special memorial-name candidates included some from the Later Jin Tianfu era.

sentences.zh: 凡士貢於鄉而屢絀於禮部，或廷試所不錄者，積前後舉數，參其年而差等之，遇親策士則別籍其名以奏，徑許附試，故曰特奏名。

translations.literal: Generally, scholars recommended in the districts but repeatedly failing at the Ministry of Rites, or not recorded in court examinations, had prior attempts and age considered by rank; at imperial questioning their names were separately registered and memorialized, directly permitted to join the examination—hence called special memorial name.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who failed repeatedly at the Ministry or in court examinations had prior attempts and age weighed; at imperial questioning their names were separately registered for direct admission—hence special memorial name.

sentences.zh: 又賜河北進士、諸科三百五十人及第、同出身。

translations.literal: Degrees and equivalent degrees were also granted to three hundred fifty jinshi and specialized candidates from Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Degrees and equivalent degrees were also granted to three hundred fifty Hebei jinshi and specialized candidates.

sentences.zh: 既下第，願試武藝及量才錄用者，又五百餘人，悉賜裝錢慰遣之，命禮部敘為一舉。

translations.literal: Those who failed but wished to test military arts or be appointed by measured talent—more than five hundred—were all given travel money and sent off; the Ministry of Rites counted it as one attempt.
translations.idiomatic: Over five hundred who failed but wished to test military arts or be appointed by talent received travel money and departure; the Ministry counted it as one attempt.

sentences.zh: 較藝之詳，推恩之廣，近代所未有也。

translations.literal: Such detailed comparison of arts and such breadth of grace—in recent times there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: The detail of comparison and breadth of imperial grace were unmatched in recent times.

sentences.zh: 舊制，及第即命以官。

translations.literal: Under the old system, receiving a degree meant immediate appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system a degree meant immediate appointment.

sentences.zh: 上初復廷試，賜出身者亦免選，於是策名之士尤眾，雖藝不及格，悉賜同出身。

translations.literal: When the emperor first restored court examination, those granted degrees were also exempted from selection; thus degree-holders were especially numerous—even those whose arts did not qualify were all granted equivalent degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When court examination was restored, degree recipients were exempted from selection; degree-holders multiplied—even those failing qualification received equivalent degrees.

sentences.zh: 乃詔有司，凡賜同出身者並令守選，循用常調，以示甄別。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the offices: all granted equivalent degrees must await selection and follow regular promotion to show discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that all equivalent-degree recipients await selection and follow regular promotion to preserve standards.

sentences.zh: 又定令：凡試卷，封印院糊名送知舉官考定高下，復令封之送覆考所，考畢然後參校得失，不合格者，須至覆場方落。

translations.literal: Regulations were also set: examination papers were sealed by the Sealing Office with names obscured and sent to the chief examiner to determine rank; then re-sealed and sent to the review examiners; after grading, pass and fail were compared—failures were dropped only at the review session.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations required sealed papers with obscured names sent to chief and review examiners; failures were finalized only after review.

sentences.zh: 諭館閣、台省官，有請屬舉人者密以聞，隱匿不告者論罪。

translations.literal: Academy, Secretariat, and Censorate officials who solicited favor for candidates were to report secretly; concealing without report was punishable.
translations.idiomatic: Academy, Secretariat, and Censorate officials soliciting favor for candidates had to report secretly; concealment was punishable.

sentences.zh: 仍詔諸王、公主、近臣，毋得以下第親族賓客求賜科名。

translations.literal: Princes, princesses, and close ministers were also forbidden to seek degrees for failed relatives and guests.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, princesses, and close ministers were forbidden to seek degrees for failed relatives and guests.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，命有司詳定《考校進士程式》，送禮部貢院，頒之諸州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, offices were ordered to detail the Grading Procedures for Jinshi and send them to the Ministry examination compound for distribution to prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4, offices detailed Grading Procedures for Jinshi and distributed them to prefectures.

sentences.zh: 士不還鄉里而竊戶他州以應選者，嚴其法。

translations.literal: Those who did not return to their home districts but secretly registered elsewhere to take examinations faced strict penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Those who secretly registered elsewhere instead of returning home faced strict penalties.

sentences.zh: 每秋賦，自縣令佐察行義保任之，上於州；

translations.literal: Each autumn examination, magistrates and assistants first investigated conduct and guaranteed candidates, reporting upward to the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn, magistrates and assistants investigated conduct and guaranteed candidates, reporting to the prefecture;

sentences.zh: 州長貳復審察得實，然後上本道使者類試。

translations.literal: prefectural chiefs and deputies re-investigated and, finding truth, reported to the circuit commissioner for categorized examination.
translations.idiomatic: prefectural chiefs re-investigated and reported to circuit commissioners for categorized examination.

sentences.zh: 已保任而有缺行，則州縣皆坐罪；

translations.literal: If guaranteed candidates later showed deficient conduct, prefectures and counties were all punished;
translations.idiomatic: If guaranteed candidates later showed deficient conduct, prefectures and counties were punished;

sentences.zh: 若省試而文理紕繆，坐元考官。

translations.literal: if at the provincial examination reasoning and wording were confused, the original examiners were punished.
translations.idiomatic: if provincial examination papers showed confused reasoning, original examiners were punished.

sentences.zh: 諸州解試額多而中者少，則不必足額。

translations.literal: If a prefecture's qualifying quota was large but passers few, the quota need not be filled.
translations.idiomatic: If qualifying quotas exceeded passers, quotas need not be filled.

sentences.zh: 尋又定《親試進士條製》。

translations.literal: Soon Regulations for Imperial Jinshi Examination were also set.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Regulations for Imperial Jinshi Examination were also established.

sentences.zh: 凡策士，即殿兩廡張帟，列幾席，標姓名其上。

translations.literal: For policy questioning, curtains were hung in both wings of the hall, with desks arranged and names marked above.
translations.idiomatic: For policy questioning, curtains hung in both hall wings with desks bearing candidates' names.

sentences.zh: 先一日表其次序，揭示闕外，翌旦拜闕下，仍入就席。

translations.literal: One day beforehand the seating order was posted outside the gate; the next morning they bowed below the gate and took their seats.
translations.idiomatic: Seating order was posted a day ahead; candidates bowed at the gate next morning and took their seats.

sentences.zh: 試卷，內臣收之，付編排官，去其卷首鄉貫狀，別以字號第之；

translations.literal: Papers were collected by inner attendants and handed to arranging officials; native-place registers at the head were removed and replaced with code numbers;
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants collected papers; native-place registers were removed and replaced with code numbers;

sentences.zh: 付封彌官謄寫校勘，用禦書院印，付考官定等畢，復封彌送覆考官再定等。

translations.literal: given to sealing officials for copying and proofreading with the Imperial Script Academy seal, then to examiners for grading; after grading, re-sealed and sent to review examiners for re-grading.
translations.idiomatic: sealing officials copied and proofread with the Imperial Script Academy seal; examiners graded, then review examiners re-graded.

sentences.zh: 編排官閱其同異，未同者再考之；

translations.literal: Arranging officials compared differences; if still unmatched, re-examined;
translations.idiomatic: Arranging officials compared results; unmatched papers were re-examined;

sentences.zh: 如復不同，即以相附近者為定。

translations.literal: if still different, the nearest ranks were taken as final.
translations.idiomatic: persistent differences were resolved by nearest rank.

sentences.zh: 始取鄉貫狀字號合之，即第其姓名、差次，並試卷以聞。

translations.literal: Native-place registers and code numbers were then matched, names and order determined, and papers submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Registers and codes were matched, names and order fixed, and papers submitted.

sentences.zh: 其考第之製凡五等：學識優長、詞理精絕為第一；

translations.literal: Grading had five levels: learning and insight superior, reasoning and diction exquisite—first rank;
translations.idiomatic: Grading had five levels: superior learning and exquisite reasoning—first;

sentences.zh: 才思該通、文理周率為第二；

translations.literal: talent comprehensive, reasoning and text thorough—second rank;
translations.idiomatic: comprehensive talent and thorough reasoning—second;

sentences.zh: 文理俱通為第三；

translations.literal: reasoning and text both pass—third rank;
translations.idiomatic: reasoning and text both adequate—third;

sentences.zh: 文理中平為第四；

translations.literal: reasoning and text middling—fourth rank;
translations.idiomatic: middling reasoning and text—fourth;

sentences.zh: 文理疏淺為第五。

translations.literal: reasoning and text shallow—fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: shallow reasoning and text—fifth.

sentences.zh: 然後臨軒唱第，上二等曰及第，三等曰出身，四等、五等曰同出身。

translations.literal: Then names were announced at the throne: first two ranks called passed; third rank called degree; fourth and fifth called equivalent degree.
translations.idiomatic: Names were announced at the throne: top two ranks passed; third received a degree; fourth and fifth equivalent degrees.

sentences.zh: 餘如貢院舊制。

translations.literal: The rest followed examination compound precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Other procedures followed compound precedent.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔士曾預南省試者，犯公罪聽贖罰。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict permitted scholars who had previously taken the southern provincial examination to redeem public offenses by fine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, prior southern provincial examinees could redeem public offenses by fine.

sentences.zh: 令禮部取前後詔令經久可行者，編為條製。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites was ordered to compile enduring edicts into regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites compiled enduring edicts into regulations.

sentences.zh: 諸科三場內有十“不”、進士詞理紕繆者各一人以上，監試、考試官從違製失論，幕職、州縣官得代日殿一選，京朝官降監場務，嚐監當則與遠地；

translations.literal: If specialized categories had ten "failures" in three sessions or jinshi had confused reasoning—one person or more—supervising and examining officials were punished for violation; local and capital officials faced demotion or remote assignment;
translations.idiomatic: Ten failures in specialized categories or confused jinshi reasoning triggered penalties for supervisors and examiners; local and capital officials faced demotion or remote assignment;

sentences.zh: 有三人，則監試、考試官亦從違製失論，幕職、州縣官衝替，京朝官遠地監當；

translations.literal: with three persons, supervising and examining officials were also punished; local officials replaced, capital officials assigned remotely;
translations.idiomatic: three failures triggered replacement of local officials and remote assignment for capital officials;

sentences.zh: 有五人，則監試以下皆停見任；

translations.literal: with five persons, all supervisors and below were suspended;
translations.idiomatic: five failures suspended all supervisors and below;

sentences.zh: 舉送守倅，諸科五十人以上有一人十“不”，即罰銅與免殿選監當，進士詞理紕繆亦如之。

translations.literal: recommending prefects and assistants—with fifty or more specialized candidates and one ten-failure, copper fines and barred sessions applied; jinshi confused reasoning likewise.
translations.idiomatic: recommending prefects faced fines if one in fifty specialized candidates had ten failures; jinshi confused reasoning likewise.

sentences.zh: 後又詔：“試鎖廳者，州長吏先校試合格，始聽取解；

translations.literal: Later an edict said: "For locked-hall candidates, prefectural chiefs must first examine and qualify before permitting submission;
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict required: "For locked-hall candidates, prefectural chiefs must pre-examine before submission;

sentences.zh: 至禮部不及格，停其官，而考試及舉送者，皆重置罪。”

translations.literal: if they failed at the Ministry of Rites, their offices were suspended and examiners and recommenders heavily punished."
translations.idiomatic: if they failed at the Ministry of Rites, their offices were suspended and examiners and recommenders heavily punished."

sentences.zh: 八年，始置謄錄院，令封印官封試卷付之，集書吏錄本，監以內侍二人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, a Transcription Office was first established; sealing officials sealed papers and handed them to clerks for copying under supervision of two inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year a Transcription Office was established; sealed papers were copied under two inner attendants' supervision.

sentences.zh: 詔：“進士第一人，令金吾司給七人導從，聽引兩節。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The top jinshi shall be given seven ushers by the Golden Guard, permitted two ceremonial staffs.
translations.idiomatic: "An edict granted the top jinshi seven ushers from the Golden Guard and two ceremonial staffs.

sentences.zh: 著為令。”

translations.literal: This was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This became regulation."

sentences.zh: 天聖初，宋興六十有二載，天下乂安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, Song had stood sixty-two years and the realm was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiansheng, after sixty-two years of Song, the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 時取才唯進士、諸科為最廣，名卿钜公，皆繇此選，而仁宗亦向用之，登上第者不數年，輒赫然顯貴矣。

translations.literal: Talent was drawn most broadly from jinshi and specialized categories; renowned ministers and great officials all came through this path, and Emperor Renzong also favored them—those receiving top ranks became conspicuously eminent within years.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi and specialized categories supplied the broadest talent; great ministers rose through them, and Emperor Renzong favored top graduates—many became eminent within years.

sentences.zh: 其貢禮部而數詘者，得特奏名，或因循不學，乃詔曰：“學猶殖也，不學將落，遜誌務時敏，厥修乃來。

translations.literal: Those who failed repeatedly at the Ministry received special memorial names; some neglected study, prompting an edict: "Learning is like cultivation—without it one declines; cultivate diligence and timely effort and improvement will come.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated Ministry failures brought special memorial names; some neglected study, prompting an edict: "Learning is cultivation—neglect it and you decline; cultivate diligence and improvement will come.

sentences.zh: 朕慮天下之士或有遺也，既已臨軒較得失，而憂其屢不中科，則衰邁而無所成，退不能返其裏閭，而進不得預於祿仕。

translations.literal: We fear scholars may be overlooked; having compared gains and losses at the throne, we worry that repeated failure leaves them aged without achievement—unable to return home in honor or advance to salary and office.
translations.idiomatic: We fear overlooked scholars; having tested them at court, we worry repeated failure leaves them aged without achievement—unable to return home or enter office.

sentences.zh: 故常數之外，特為之甄采。

translations.literal: Therefore beyond the regular quota we specially select them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore beyond the regular quota we specially select them.

sentences.zh: 而狃於寬恩，遂隳素業，苟簡成風，甚可恥也。

translations.literal: Yet accustomed to lenient grace, they ruin their proper studies; perfunctory custom takes shape—most shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet accustomed to leniency, they abandon proper study—a shameful perfunctory custom.

sentences.zh: 自今宜篤進厥學，無習僥幸焉。”

translations.literal: From now on earnestly advance your learning and do not rely on luck."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth advance your learning earnestly and do not rely on luck."

sentences.zh: 時晏殊言：“唐明經並試策問，參其所習，以取材識短長。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Shu said: "Tang Classics Understanding also tested policy questions, weighing what candidates had studied to measure knowledge and insight.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu said: "Tang Classics Understanding also tested policy questions to measure knowledge.

sentences.zh: 今諸科專記誦，非取士之意，請終場試策一篇。”

translations.literal: Now specialized categories rely only on memorization—not the intent of selecting scholars; please test one policy essay at the final session."
translations.idiomatic: Now specialized categories rely on memorization alone—not true selection; test one policy essay at the final session."

sentences.zh: 詔近臣議之，咸謂諸科非所習，議遂寢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered close ministers to discuss; all said specialized categories were not their field of study—the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Close ministers discussed; all said specialized categories were outside their study—the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 舊制，鎖廳試落輒停官，至是始詔免罪。

translations.literal: Under the old system, locked-hall failures always meant office suspension; now an edict first exempted punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Locked-hall failure had meant office suspension; now punishment was first exempted.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，詔曰：“鄉學之士益蕃，而取人路狹，使孤寒棲遲，或老而不得進，朕甚憫之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyou, an edict said: "District scholars grow ever more numerous while the path narrows, leaving the isolated and poor stalled—some aging without advancement; We pity them.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingyou's start an edict said: "District scholars multiply while paths narrow, leaving the poor stalled—We pity them.

sentences.zh: 其令南省就試進士、諸科，十取其二。

translations.literal: Let the southern provincial examination for jinshi and specialized categories take two from ten.
translations.idiomatic: Let jinshi and specialized provincial examinations take two from ten.

sentences.zh: 凡年五十，進士五舉、諸科六舉；

translations.literal: All age fifty with five jinshi or six specialized attempts;
translations.idiomatic: Age fifty with five jinshi or six specialized attempts;

sentences.zh: 嚐經殿試，進士三舉、諸科五舉；

translations.literal: those who had undergone palace examination with three jinshi or five specialized attempts;
translations.idiomatic: prior palace examination with three jinshi or five specialized attempts;

sentences.zh: 及嚐預先朝禦試，雖試文不合格，毋輒黜，皆以名聞。”

translations.literal: and those who had previously taken earlier imperial examinations—even if papers failed—were not dismissed but all reported by name."
translations.idiomatic: and prior imperial examinees—even if papers failed—were reported by name without dismissal."

sentences.zh: 自此率以為常。

translations.literal: From this it became regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: This became regular practice.

sentences.zh: 士有親戚仕本州，或為發解官，及侍親遠宦，距本州二千里，令轉運司類試，以十率之，取三人。

translations.literal: If a scholar had relatives serving in his prefecture or a recommending official there, or served parents far away more than two thousand li from home, the transport commissioner categorized and examined them—three from ten.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars with relatives serving locally or parents far away beyond two thousand li were examined by transport commissioners—three from ten.

sentences.zh: 於是諸路始有別頭試。

translations.literal: Thereupon separate-head examinations began in the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Separate-head examinations began in the circuits.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔開封府、國子監及別頭試，封彌、謄錄如禮部。

translations.literal: That year Kaifeng, the Directorate, and separate-head examinations sealed and transcribed like the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: That year Kaifeng, the Directorate, and separate-head exams sealed and transcribed like the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 初，貢士踵唐製，猶用公卷，然多假他人文字，或傭人書之。

translations.literal: At first candidates still used public portfolios as in Tang, but many used others' writing or hired scribes.
translations.idiomatic: At first candidates still submitted public portfolios as in Tang, but many used ghostwriters or hired scribes.

sentences.zh: 景德中，嚐限舉人於試紙前親書家狀，如公卷及後所試書體不同，並駁放；

translations.literal: In Jingde, candidates were required to personally write household registers on examination paper; if handwriting differed from public portfolio or later papers, they were rejected;
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde candidates had to handwrite household registers on exam paper; handwriting mismatches meant rejection;

sentences.zh: 其假手文字，辨之得實，即斥去，永不得赴舉。

translations.literal: if ghostwriting was proven, they were expelled and forever barred.
translations.idiomatic: proven ghostwriting meant permanent expulsion.

sentences.zh: 賈昌朝言：“自唐以來，禮部采名譽，觀素學，故預投公卷；

translations.literal: Jia Changchao said: "Since Tang, the Ministry gathered reputation and observed prior learning, hence public portfolios;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Changchao said: "Since Tang the Ministry valued reputation and prior learning, hence public portfolios;

sentences.zh: 今有封彌、謄錄法，一切考諸試篇，則公卷可罷。”

translations.literal: now with sealing and transcription, everything is tested through examination papers—public portfolios may be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: now with sealing and transcription, everything rests on exam papers—public portfolios may be abolished."

sentences.zh: 自是不復有公卷。

translations.literal: From this time public portfolios ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Public portfolios ceased thereafter.

sentences.zh: 寶元中，李淑侍經筵，上訪以進士詩、賦、策、論先後，俾以故事對。

translations.literal: In Baoyuan, Li Shu attended the classics lecture; the emperor asked the order of jinshi poetry, rhapsody, policy, and discourse essays, and he answered by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyuan, Li Shu attended the classics lecture; the emperor asked the order of jinshi exam sections and he answered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 淑對曰：“唐調露二年，劉思立為考功員外郎，以進士試策滅裂，請帖經以觀其學，試雜文以觀其才。

translations.literal: Shu replied: "In Tang Tiaolu 2, Liu Sili as Director of Personnel found jinshi policy answers careless and requested fill-in classics to observe learning and mixed essays to observe talent.
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied: "In Tang Tiaolu 2, Liu Sili requested fill-in classics and mixed essays when policy answers proved careless.

sentences.zh: 自此沿以為常。

translations.literal: From this it became regular.
translations.idiomatic: This became regular practice.

sentences.zh: 至永隆二年，進士試雜文二篇，通文律者，始試策。

translations.literal: By Yonglong 2, jinshi tested two mixed essays; those passing literary rules then tested policy.
translations.idiomatic: By Yonglong 2 jinshi tested two mixed essays before policy.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一年，進士試一經，能通者試文賦，又通而後試策，五條皆通，中第。

translations.literal: In Tianbao 11, jinshi tested one classic; those passing tested literary rhapsody, then policy; all five policy questions passing meant success.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 11 one classic, then rhapsody, then policy—all five policy passes meant success.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，趙讚請試以時務策五篇，箴、論、表、讚各一篇，以代詩、賦。

translations.literal: In Jianzhong 2, Zhao Zan requested five current-affairs policy essays plus memorial, discourse, petition, and eulogy each replacing poetry and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2 Zhao Zan proposed policy essays and formal prose replacing poetry and rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，試帖經，略問大義，取精通者，次試論、議各一篇。

translations.literal: In Dahe 3, fill-in classics with brief meaning questions tested mastery; then one discourse and one deliberation essay.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 3 fill-in classics and brief meaning questions preceded discourse and deliberation essays.

sentences.zh: 八年，禮部試以帖經口義，次試策五篇，問經義者三，問時務者二。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Ministry tested fill-in oral meaning, then five policy questions—three on classics, two on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year fill-in oral meaning preceded five policy questions—three classics, two current affairs.

sentences.zh: 厥後變易，遂以詩賦為第一場，論第二場，策第三場，帖經第四場。

translations.literal: Later changes made poetry-rhapsody the first session, discourse second, policy third, fill-in classics fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Later changes made poetry-rhapsody first, discourse second, policy third, fill-in classics fourth.

sentences.zh: 今陛下欲求理道而不以雕琢為貴，得取士之實矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty seeks the Way without prizing ornament—You have the reality of selecting scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty seeks the Way without prizing ornament—you have true selection of scholars.

sentences.zh: 然考官以所試分考，不能通加評校，而每場輒退落，士之中否，殆係於幸不幸。

translations.literal: Yet examiners grade each session separately without overall comparison; each session eliminates candidates—success or failure hangs on fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Yet examiners grade sessions separately; each eliminates candidates—success hangs too much on fortune.

sentences.zh: 願約舊制，先策，次論，次賦及詩，次帖經、墨義，而敕有司並試四場，通較工拙，毋以一場得失為去留。”

translations.literal: Please restore the old order: policy first, then discourse, then rhapsody and poetry, then fill-in and written interpretation—and order offices to test all four sessions together, comparing overall merit without eliminating on one session alone."
translations.idiomatic: Please restore old order—policy, discourse, rhapsody and poetry, fill-in and interpretation—and compare all four sessions together without eliminating on one alone."

sentences.zh: 詔有司議，稍施行焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered offices to discuss; it was partially implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Offices discussed and partially implemented it.

sentences.zh: 既而知制誥富弼言曰：“國家沿隋、唐設進士科，自咸平、景德以來，為法尤密，而得人之道，或有未至。

translations.literal: Then Drafting Officer Fu Bi said: "The state follows Sui and Tang in establishing jinshi; since Xianping and Jingde the method has been especially strict, yet the path to obtaining men may not have reached perfection.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Officer Fu Bi said: "Since Xianping and Jingde jinshi rules have been strict, yet selection may not have reached perfection.

sentences.zh: 且曆代取士，悉委有司，未聞天子親試也。

translations.literal: In successive dynasties selection was entrusted to offices; never before did the Son of Heaven personally examine.
translations.idiomatic: Selection was always entrusted to offices; the Son of Heaven never personally examined.

sentences.zh: 至唐武後始有殿試，何足取哉？

translations.literal: Only under Empress Wu did palace examination appear—what is there to emulate?
translations.idiomatic: Only under Empress Wu did palace examination appear—what is there to emulate?

sentences.zh: 使禮部次高下以奏，而引諸殿廷，唱名賜第，則與殿試無以異矣。”

translations.literal: Let the Ministry rank and report, then summon to the hall for name announcement and degree bestowal—how is that different from palace examination?
translations.idiomatic: Let the Ministry rank and report, then announce names at court—how differs that from palace examination?"

sentences.zh: 遂詔罷殿試。

translations.literal: An edict then abolished palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished palace examination.

sentences.zh: 而議者多言其輕上恩，隳故事，復如舊。

translations.literal: Critics said it slighted imperial grace and ruined precedent; it was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said it slighted imperial grace; palace examination was restored.

sentences.zh: 時範仲淹參知政事，意欲復古勸學，數言興學校，本行實。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan as Vice Grand Councillor wished to restore antiquity and encourage learning, repeatedly urging schools and practical conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Fan Zhongyan sought to restore antiquity, urging schools and practical conduct.

sentences.zh: 詔近臣議，於是宋祁等奏：“教不本於學校，士不察於鄉里，則不能核名實。

translations.literal: Close ministers were ordered to discuss; Song Qi and others memorialized: "If teaching does not root in schools and scholars are not examined in districts, names and reality cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi and others memorialized: "Without school-based teaching and district examination, names and reality cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 有司束以聲病，學者專於記誦，則不足盡人材。

translations.literal: If offices bind candidates to tonal rules and scholars specialize in memorization, human talent cannot be fully revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Binding candidates to tonal rules and memorization cannot reveal full talent.

sentences.zh: 參考眾說，擇其便於今者，莫若使士皆土著，而教之於學校，然後州縣察其履行，則學者修飭矣。”

translations.literal: Considering all proposals, the best present course is to require local residence and school education, then have prefectures and counties examine conduct—then scholars will be disciplined."
translations.idiomatic: The best course is local residence, school education, and conduct examination by prefectures and counties."

sentences.zh: 乃詔州縣立學，士須在學三百日，乃聽預秋賦，舊嚐充賦者百日而止。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties were ordered to establish schools; scholars needed three hundred days of study before autumn examination; prior examinees needed only one hundred.
