translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties established schools; three hundred study days were required before autumn exams; prior examinees needed one hundred.

sentences.zh: 試於州者，令相保任，有匿服、犯刑、虧行、冒名等禁。

translations.literal: Prefectural testers required mutual guarantee with prohibitions on concealed mourning, criminal offense, deficient conduct, and false identity.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural testing required mutual guarantee with bans on concealed mourning, crime, bad conduct, and false identity.

sentences.zh: 三場：先策，次論，次詩賦，通考為去取，而罷帖經、墨義，士通經術願對大義者，試十道。

translations.literal: Three sessions: policy first, discourse second, poetry-rhapsody third; overall pass determined selection; fill-in and written interpretation abolished; those versed in classics could test ten great-meaning questions.
translations.idiomatic: Three sessions—policy, discourse, poetry-rhapsody—determined selection; fill-in and written interpretation were abolished; classicists could test ten great-meaning questions.

sentences.zh: 仲淹既去，而執政意皆異。

translations.literal: After Fan Zhongyan departed, those in power all differed.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Zhongyan departed, the ruling faction disagreed.

sentences.zh: 是冬，詔罷入學日限。

translations.literal: That winter an edict abolished the school-day requirement.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the school-day requirement was abolished.

sentences.zh: 言初令不便者甚眾，以為詩賦聲病易考，而策論汗漫難知；

translations.literal: Many said the initial order was inconvenient—poetry-rhapsody tonal rules were easy to grade while policy discourse was boundless and hard to judge;
translations.idiomatic: Many protested—poetry-rhapsody tonal rules were easy to grade while policy discourse was hard to judge;

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，莫之有改，且得人嚐多矣。

translations.literal: since founding ancestors there had been no change, and many worthy men had been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: since the founding ancestors the system had produced many worthy men.

sentences.zh: 天子下其議，有司請如舊法。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the discussion down; offices requested return to the old method.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the matter down; offices requested the old method.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：“科舉舊條，皆先朝所定也，宜一切如故，前所更定令悉罷。”

translations.literal: An edict then said: "Examination regulations were all set by former courts and should all remain as before; all recently changed orders are abolished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Examination regulations set by former courts should all remain; recent changes are abolished."

sentences.zh: 會張方平知貢舉，言：“文章之變與政通。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fangping served as chief examiner he said: "Literary change keeps pace with governance.
translations.idiomatic: Chief examiner Zhang Fangping said: "Literary change keeps pace with governance.

sentences.zh: 今設科選才，專取辭藝，士惟道義積於中，英華發於外，然則以文取士，所以叩諸外而質其中之蘊也。

translations.literal: Now in selecting talent by examination, taking only literary skill—if scholars store the Way within and brilliance emerges without, then taking scholars by writing is to knock on the outside and verify inner substance.
translations.idiomatic: Selecting by literary skill alone assumes inner substance shows in writing—yet words without measure reveal nothing.

sentences.zh: 言而不度，則何觀焉。

translations.literal: Words without measure—what is there to observe?
translations.idiomatic: Words without measure reveal nothing.

sentences.zh: 邇來文格日失其舊，各出新意，相勝為奇。

translations.literal: Recently literary style daily loses its old form; each devises new ideas, competing in novelty.
translations.idiomatic: Recently literary style loses its old form as each competes in novelty.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惡其然，屢下詔書戒飭，而學者樂於放逸，罕能自還。

translations.literal: The court detests this and repeatedly issues edicts of warning, yet scholars delight in unrestraint and rarely return.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly warns against this, yet scholars delight in unrestraint.

sentences.zh: 今賦或八百字，論或千餘字，策或置所問而妄肆胸臆，漫陳他事，驅扇浮薄，重虧雅俗，豈取賢斂才備治具之意邪？

translations.literal: Now rhapsodies reach eight hundred characters, discourses over a thousand, policy essays ignore questions and rashly expound other matters—driving frivolity and harming refined custom—is this the intent of gathering the worthy and preparing instruments of governance?
translations.idiomatic: Rhapsodies reach eight hundred characters, discourses over a thousand, policy essays ignore the questions—is this gathering the worthy?

sentences.zh: 其增習新體，澶漫不合程式，悉已考落，請申前詔，揭而示之。”」

translations.literal: Those who practiced new styles, diffuse and not conforming to form, have all been failed; please reissue the prior edict and display it.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates in diffuse new styles have been failed; please reissue the prior edict publicly."

sentences.zh: 初，禮部奏名，以四百名爲限，又諸科雜問大義，僥倖之人，悉以爲不便。

translations.literal: At first Ministry registration was capped at four hundred names; specialized categories also tested great meaning—opportunists all found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry registration was capped at four hundred; great-meaning tests for specialized categories displeased opportunists.

sentences.zh: 知制誥王珪奏曰：“唐自貞觀訖開元，文章最盛，較藝者歲千餘人，而所收無幾。

translations.literal: Drafting Officer Wang Gui memorialized: "From Tang Zhenguan through Kaiyuan, literature flourished most; yearly comparers numbered over a thousand yet admissions were few.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui memorialized: "From Zhenguan through Kaiyuan literature flourished; thousands competed yearly yet few passed.

sentences.zh: 咸亨、上元增其數，亦不及百人。

translations.literal: Xianheng and Shangyuan increased numbers yet still did not reach one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Xianheng and Shangyuan increased quotas yet still admitted fewer than one hundred.

sentences.zh: 國初取士，大抵唐製，逮興國中，貢舉之路浸廣，無有定數。

translations.literal: At founding, selection largely followed Tang; by Xingguo the tribute path widened without fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Early selection followed Tang; by Xingguo the tribute path widened without fixed numbers.

sentences.zh: 比年官吏猥眾，故近詔限四百人，以懲其弊。

translations.literal: In recent years officials grew numerous, so a recent edict capped at four hundred to punish abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Recent edicts capped admissions at four hundred to curb swollen ranks.

sentences.zh: 且進士、明經先經義而後試策，三試皆通為中第，大略與進士等，而諸科既不問經義，又無策試，止以誦數精粗為中否，則其專固不達於理，安足以長民冶事哉？

translations.literal: Jinshi and Classics Understanding first test classic meaning then policy; three sessions all passing equals jinshi—but specialized categories without classic meaning or policy test only memorization precision—is this sufficient to govern people and affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi test classic meaning then policy; specialized categories test only memorization—is that enough to govern people?

sentences.zh: 前詔諸科終場問本經大義十道，《九經》、《五經》科止問義而不責記誦，皆以著於令。

translations.literal: The prior edict required ten great-meaning questions on original classics at final session for specialized categories; Nine and Five Classics asked meaning not memorization—all fixed in regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Prior edicts required ten great-meaning questions on original classics; Nine and Five Classics tested meaning not memorization.

sentences.zh: 言者以為難於遽更，而圖安於弊也。

translations.literal: Critics said sudden change was hard; they sought comfort in abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called sudden change hard and clung to old abuses.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下申敕有司，固守是法，毋輕易焉。”

translations.literal: Only let Your Majesty instruct offices to hold firm and not change lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Only let Your Majesty instruct offices to hold firm and not change lightly."

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，親試舉人，凡與殿試者始免黜落。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, the emperor personally examined candidates; all who reached palace examination were first exempted from dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 2 all who reached palace examination were first exempted from dismissal.

sentences.zh: 時進士益相習為奇僻，鉤章棘句，浸失渾淳。

translations.literal: Jinshi increasingly practiced eccentric phrasing and thorny clauses, gradually losing natural simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi increasingly wrote eccentric, thorny prose, losing natural simplicity.

sentences.zh: 歐陽脩知貢舉，尤以為患，痛裁抑之，仍嚴禁挾書者。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu as chief examiner especially deplored this, sternly suppressing it while forbidding hidden texts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief examiner Ouyang Xiu sternly suppressed eccentric prose and forbidden texts.

sentences.zh: 既而試榜出，時所推譽，皆不在選。

translations.literal: When results posted, celebrated candidates were mostly not selected.
translations.idiomatic: When results posted, celebrated candidates were mostly excluded.

sentences.zh: 澆薄之士，候脩晨朝，群聚詆斥之，街司邏卒不能止，至為祭文投其家，卒不能求其主名置於法，然自是文體亦少變。

translations.literal: Frivolous scholars waited for Xiu's morning audience and gathered to denounce him; street patrols could not stop them; sacrificial essays were thrown at his home yet the ringleader could not be found and punished—yet from this literary style somewhat changed.
translations.idiomatic: Furious scholars denounced Xiu at court; sacrificial essays were thrown at his home—yet literary style somewhat changed.

sentences.zh: 待試京師者恒六七千人，一不幸有故不應詔，往往沉淪十數年，以此毀行幹進者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Those awaiting examination in the capital often numbered six or seven thousand; one misfortune preventing response to the summons often meant stagnation over ten years—those who ruined conduct to advance were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven thousand awaited capital examination; one missed summons could mean ten years' stagnation—countless ruined conduct to advance.

sentences.zh: 王洙侍邇英閣講《周禮》，至“三年大比，大考州裏，以讚鄉大夫廢興。”

translations.literal: Wang Zhu attended the Classics lecture on the Zhou Rites passage: "Every three years a great comparison; examine states and districts to assist district grandees in promotion and demotion."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu lectured on the Zhou Rites: "Every three years compare and examine districts to assist promotion and demotion."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“古者選士如此，今率四五歲一下詔，故士有抑而不得進者，孰若裁其數而屢舉也。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ancient selection was thus; now edicts come every four or five years, so scholars are suppressed without advancement—would it not be better to cut numbers and examine frequently?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Ancient selection was thus; now edicts come every four or five years—would it not be better to cut numbers and examine more often?"

sentences.zh: 下有司議，鹹請：“易以間歲之法，則無滯才之歎。

translations.literal: Offices were ordered to discuss; all requested: "Change to biennial method and the lament of stalled talent will cease.
translations.idiomatic: Offices requested: "A biennial method would end stalled talent.

sentences.zh: 薦舉數既減半，主司易以詳較，得士必精。

translations.literal: With halved recommendations, chief examiners can compare carefully and obtain finer scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Halved recommendations let examiners compare carefully for finer scholars.

sentences.zh: 且人少則有司易於檢察，偽濫自不能容，使寒苦藝學之人得進。”

translations.literal: Fewer candidates let offices inspect easily; fraud cannot remain; poor diligent scholars of arts can advance."
translations.idiomatic: Fewer candidates ease inspection, curb fraud, and let poor diligent scholars advance."

sentences.zh: 於是下詔：“間歲貢舉，進士、諸科悉解舊額之半。

translations.literal: An edict then said: "Biennial tribute-recommendation—jinshi and specialized categories all reduce old quotas by half.
translations.idiomatic: "An edict ordered biennial tribute with jinshi and specialized quotas halved.

sentences.zh: 增設明經，試法：凡明兩經或三經、五經，各問大義十條，兩經通八，三經通六，五經通五為合格，兼以《論語》、《孝經》，策時務三條，出身與進士等。

translations.literal: Add Classics Understanding examination: for two or three or five classics, ten great-meaning questions each; two classics require eight passes, three require six, five require five; plus Analects and Classic of Filial Piety and three current-affairs policy questions—degree equal to jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Classics Understanding was added: two, three, or five classics with ten great-meaning questions each; Analects and Filial Piety plus three policy questions—degree equal to jinshi.

sentences.zh: 而罷說書舉。”

translations.literal: The Lecturer Examination was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Lecturer Examination was abolished."

sentences.zh: 時以科舉既數，而高第之人驟顯，欲稍裁抑。

translations.literal: At the time, because examinations were frequent and top graduates rose swiftly, some wished to restrain this.
translations.idiomatic: Because examinations were frequent and top graduates rose swiftly, some wished restraint.

sentences.zh: 遂詔曰：“朕惟國之取士，與士之待舉，不可曠而冗也。

translations.literal: An edict then said: "We consider that state selection and scholars awaiting examination must not be neglected yet must not be redundant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "State selection and scholars awaiting examination must neither be neglected nor redundant.

sentences.zh: 故立間歲之期，以勵其勤；

translations.literal: Therefore establish biennial periods to encourage diligence;
translations.idiomatic: Biennial periods encourage diligence;

sentences.zh: 約貢舉之數，以精其選。

translations.literal: reduce tribute numbers to refine selection.
translations.idiomatic: reduced tribute numbers refine selection.

sentences.zh: 著為定式，申敕有司，而高第之人，嚐不次而用。

translations.literal: Fix this as permanent form and instruct offices—yet top graduates are often appointed out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fix this permanently—yet top graduates are often appointed out of turn.

sentences.zh: 若循舊比，終至濫官，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: If following old ratios, offices will eventually be flooded—most meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: Following old ratios would flood offices—meaningless.

sentences.zh: 自今製科入第三等，與進士第一，除大理評事、簽書兩使幕職官；

translations.literal: From now special decree third rank equals jinshi first—appointed Case Reviewer and fan administration secretary;
translations.idiomatic: Special decree third rank equals jinshi first—Case Reviewer and fan secretary;

sentences.zh: 代還，升通判；

translations.literal: after term, promoted to vice commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: after term, vice commissioner;

sentences.zh: 再任滿，試館職。

translations.literal: after second full term, tested for academy post.
translations.idiomatic: after second term, tested for academy post.

sentences.zh: 製科入第四等，與進士第二、第三，除兩使幕職官；

translations.literal: Special decree fourth rank equals jinshi second and third—fan administration secretary;
translations.idiomatic: Special decree fourth equals jinshi second and third—fan secretary;

sentences.zh: 代還，改次等京官。

translations.literal: after term, promoted to next-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: after term, next-rank capital official.

sentences.zh: 製科入第五等，與進士第四、第五，除試銜知縣；

translations.literal: Special decree fifth equals jinshi fourth and fifth—trial magistrate with nominal rank;
translations.idiomatic: Special decree fifth equals jinshi fourth and fifth—trial magistrate;

sentences.zh: 代還，遷兩使職官。

translations.literal: after term, promoted to fan administration official.
translations.idiomatic: after term, fan administration official.

sentences.zh: 鎖廳人視此。

translations.literal: Locked-hall candidates follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Locked-hall candidates follow this.

sentences.zh: 若夫高才異行，施於有政而功狀較然者，當以異恩擢焉。”

translations.literal: For outstanding talent and unusual conduct with proven administrative merit, special promotion applies.
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding talent with proven merit receives special promotion."

sentences.zh: 仁宗之朝十有三舉，進士四千五百七十人；

translations.literal: In Emperor Renzong's reign there were thirteen sessions and four thousand five hundred seventy jinshi;
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's thirteen sessions there were four thousand five hundred seventy jinshi;

sentences.zh: 其甲第之三人凡三十有九，其後不至於公卿者，五人而已。

translations.literal: of thirty-nine top-three graduates in all, only five did not reach chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: of thirty-nine top-three graduates, only five failed to reach chief minister rank.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，議者以間歲貢士法不便。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, critics said biennial tribute was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne, critics said biennial tribute was inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 乃詔禮部三歲一貢舉，天下解額，取未行間歲之前四之三為率，明經、諸科毋過進士之數。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ministry tribute every three years; nationwide qualifying quotas took three-fourths of pre-biennial rates; Classics Understanding and specialized categories not exceeding jinshi numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry tribute every three years was ordered; quotas took three-fourths of pre-biennial rates.

sentences.zh: 神宗篤意經學，深憫貢舉之弊，且以西北人材多不在選，遂議更法。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong devoted himself to classical learning, deeply pitying tribute abuses, and because northwest talent often missed selection, reform was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong, devoted to classical learning, pitied tribute abuses and northwest talent lost to selection—reform was discussed.

sentences.zh: 王安石謂：“古之取士俱本於學，請興建學校以復古。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said: "Ancient selection all rooted in schools—please establish schools to restore antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said: "Ancient selection rooted in schools—establish schools to restore antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其明經、諸科欲行廢罷，取明經人數增進士額。”

translations.literal: Classics Understanding and specialized categories should be abolished; add Classics Understanding numbers to jinshi quota."
translations.idiomatic: Abolish specialized categories and add their numbers to jinshi quota."

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：“化民成俗，必自庠序；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Transforming people and completing custom must begin with schools;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Transforming people must begin with schools;

sentences.zh: 進賢興能，抑繇貢舉。

translations.literal: advancing the worthy and raising ability rests on tribute-recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: advancing the worthy rests on tribute-recommendation.

sentences.zh: 而四方執經藝者專於誦數，趨鄉舉者狃於文辭，與古所謂‘三物賓興，九年大成’，亦已盭矣。

translations.literal: Yet scholars holding classics specialize in recitation while examination candidates cling to literary phrasing—far from ancient 'three things to raise the worthy and nine years to complete achievement.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet classicists recite while candidates cling to phrasing—far from ancient 'three standards and nine years to completion.'

sentences.zh: 今下郡國招徠雋賢，其教育之方，課試之格，令兩製、兩省、待制以上、御史、三司、三館雜議以聞。”

translations.literal: Now summon worthy talent from prefectures; let two-administration, Secretariat, censor, fiscal, and academy officials jointly discuss education and examination methods and report."
translations.idiomatic: Summon worthy talent from prefectures; let high officials jointly discuss education and examination methods."

sentences.zh: 議者多謂變法便。

translations.literal: Most debaters said reform was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Most debaters favored reform.

sentences.zh: 直史館蘇軾曰：

translations.literal: Directorate Compiler Su Shi said:
translations.idiomatic: Directorate Compiler Su Shi said:

sentences.zh: 得人之道，在於知人，知人之法，在於責實。

translations.literal: The path to obtaining men lies in knowing men; the method of knowing men lies in requiring reality.
translations.idiomatic: Obtaining men requires knowing men; knowing men requires holding them to reality.

sentences.zh: 使君相有知人之明，朝廷有責實之政，則胥吏、皂隸，未嚐無人，雖用今之法，臣以為有餘；

translations.literal: If ruler and ministers know men and the court holds to reality, even clerks and runners may contain talent—using present methods I believe there would be surplus;
translations.idiomatic: If rulers know men and the court demands reality, even clerks may hold talent—present methods would suffice;

sentences.zh: 使無知人之明，無責實之政，則公卿、侍從，常患無人，況學校貢舉乎？

translations.literal: if there is no knowing men and no requiring reality, even grand ministers and attendants often lack men—how much less schools and tribute?
translations.idiomatic: without knowing men and demanding reality, even grand ministers lack men—how much less schools and tribute?

sentences.zh: 雖復古之制，臣以爲不足矣。

translations.literal: Even restoring ancient institutions, I believe it would be insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Even restoring ancient institutions would be insufficient.

sentences.zh: 時有可否，物有興廢，使三代聖人復生於今，其選舉亦必有道，何必由學乎？

translations.literal: Things have times of feasibility and institutions rise and fall; if sage kings of three dynasties were reborn today, their selection would also have a Way—why must it be through schools?
translations.idiomatic: If sage kings of three dynasties were reborn today, selection would have its Way—why must it pass through schools?

sentences.zh: 且慶曆間嚐立學矣，天下以為太平可待，至於今惟空名僅存。

translations.literal: Moreover in Qingli schools were once established; the realm thought peace imminent—yet until now only empty names remain.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli schools once promised peace—yet only empty names remain.

sentences.zh: 今陛下必欲求德行道藝之士，責九年大成之業，則將變今之禮，易今之俗。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly seeks men of virtue, conduct, and arts and requires nine years' completion, you must change present rites and transform present custom.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly seek men of virtue and arts and require nine years' completion, you must change present rites and custom.

sentences.zh: 又當發民力以治宮室，斂民財以養遊士，置學立師；

translations.literal: You must also mobilize the people to build palaces, collect wealth to maintain wandering scholars, establish schools and teachers;
translations.idiomatic: You must mobilize people to build palaces, collect wealth for wandering scholars, establish schools;

sentences.zh: 以又時簡不帥教者，屏之遠方，徒為紛紛，其與慶曆之際何異？

translations.literal: and from time to time expel those not following instruction to distant places—mere turmoil no different from Qingli.
translations.idiomatic: and expel the undisciplined—mere turmoil no different from Qingli.

sentences.zh: 至於貢舉，或曰鄉舉德行而略文章；

translations.literal: As for tribute, some say recommend by district virtue and slight literary skill;
translations.idiomatic: Some say recommend by district virtue and slight literary skill;

sentences.zh: 或曰專取策論而罷詩賦；

translations.literal: some say take only policy discourse and abolish poetry-rhapsody;
translations.idiomatic: some say take only policy and abolish poetry-rhapsody;

sentences.zh: 或欲舉唐故事，采譽望而罷封彌；

translations.literal: some wish to follow Tang precedent, gather reputation and abolish sealing;
translations.idiomatic: some wish to follow Tang, gather reputation and abolish sealing;

sentences.zh: 或欲變經生帖、墨而考大義，此數者皆非也。

translations.literal: some wish to change classicists' fill-in and written interpretation to test great meaning—all these are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: some wish to replace fill-in with great meaning—all wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫欲興德行，在於君人者修身以格物，審好惡以表俗，若欲設科立名以取之，則是教天下相率而為偽也。

translations.literal: To raise virtue and conduct, the ruler must cultivate self and discern likes and dislikes to set custom; if you establish categories and names to gather them, you teach the realm to compete in falsity.
translations.idiomatic: To raise virtue the ruler must cultivate self and set custom; category-based selection teaches the realm to compete in falsity.

sentences.zh: 上以孝取人，則勇者割股，怯者廬墓。

translations.literal: If the ruler selects by filial piety, the brave cut flesh from their thighs and the timid mourn at parents' graves.
translations.idiomatic: Select by filial piety and the brave cut flesh from their thighs while the timid mourn at graves.

sentences.zh: 上以廉取人，則弊車、羸馬、惡衣、菲食，凡可以中上意者無所不至。

translations.literal: If the ruler selects by integrity, broken carts, thin horses, bad clothes, and poor food—whatever may please superiors—is done without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Select by integrity and broken carts, thin horses, and poor clothes become performances of virtue.

sentences.zh: 自文章言之，則策論為有用，詩賦為無益；

translations.literal: As for writing, policy discourse is useful and poetry-rhapsody useless;
translations.idiomatic: In writing, policy is useful and poetry-rhapsody useless;

sentences.zh: 自政事言之，則詩賦、論策均為無用。

translations.literal: as for governance, both poetry-rhapsody and policy discourse are useless.
translations.idiomatic: in governance, both poetry-rhapsody and policy are useless.

sentences.zh: 然自祖宗以來莫之廢者，以為設法取士，不過如此也。

translations.literal: Yet since founding ancestors it has not been abolished—because setting methods to take scholars goes no further than this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since founding ancestors it has not been abolished—because selection methods go no further.

sentences.zh: 近世文章華麗，無如楊億。

translations.literal: In recent times none matched Yang Yi in ornate writing.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times none matched Yang Yi in ornate writing.

sentences.zh: 使億尚在，則忠清鯁亮之士也。

translations.literal: If Yi were still alive, he would be a loyal, upright, and stern gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: If Yi still lived, he would be loyal, upright, and stern.

sentences.zh: 通經學古，無如孫復、石介。

translations.literal: In mastering classics and antiquity none matched Sun Fu and Shi Jie.
translations.idiomatic: In classics and antiquity none matched Sun Fu and Shi Jie.

sentences.zh: 使復、介尚在，則迂闊誕謾之士也。

translations.literal: If Fu and Jie were still alive, they would be narrow, extravagant, and absurd gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: If Fu and Jie still lived, they would seem narrow and absurd.

sentences.zh: 矧自唐至今，以詩賦為名臣者，不可勝數，何負於天下，而必欲廢之？

translations.literal: Moreover from Tang to today renowned ministers selected by poetry-rhapsody are beyond counting—what harm to the realm that they must be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: From Tang to today countless renowned ministers came through poetry-rhapsody—why must it be abolished?

sentences.zh: 帝讀軾疏曰：“吾固疑此，得軾議，釋然矣。”

translations.literal: The emperor reading Shi's memorial said: "I indeed doubted this; receiving Shi's discussion, I am relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Reading Shi's memorial the emperor said: "I indeed doubted this; Shi's discussion relieves me."

sentences.zh: 他日問王安石，對曰：“今人材乏少，且其學術不一，異論紛然，不能一道德故也。

translations.literal: Another day he asked Wang Anshi, who replied: "Today talent is scarce and learning diverges in many unsound opinions—they cannot unify morality.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked Wang Anshi, who replied: "Talent is scarce and learning diverges—they cannot unify morality.

sentences.zh: 一道德則修學校，欲修學校，則貢舉法不可不變。

translations.literal: Unifying morality requires repairing schools; repairing schools requires changing tribute methods.
translations.idiomatic: Unifying morality requires schools; schools require changing tribute methods.

sentences.zh: 若謂此科嚐多得人，自緣仕進別無他路，其間不容無賢；

translations.literal: If you say this category often obtained many men, it is because office had no other path—among them the unworthy cannot be absent;
translations.idiomatic: If this category often obtained men, it is because office had no other path—unworthy men cannot be absent;

sentences.zh: 若謂科法已善，則未也。

translations.literal: if you say the examination law is already good, it is not yet so.
translations.idiomatic: if you say examination law is already good, it is not yet so.

sentences.zh: 今以少壯時，正當講求天下正理，乃閉門學作詩賦，及其入官，世事皆所不習，此科法敗壞人材，致不如古。”

translations.literal: Now in youth one should study the correct principles of the realm, yet they close doors to learn poetry-rhapsody; entering office they know nothing of affairs—this examination law ruins talent and falls short of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Youth should study correct principles, yet they learn poetry-rhapsody; entering office they know nothing—this law ruins talent and falls short of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 既而中書門下又言：“古之取士，皆本學校，道德一於上，習俗成於下，其人才皆足以有為於世。

translations.literal: Then the Secretariat and Chancellery also said: "Ancient selection all rooted in schools; morality unified above and custom formed below—their talent sufficed for the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat said: "Ancient selection rooted in schools produced talent sufficient for the age.

sentences.zh: 今欲追復古製，則患於無漸。

translations.literal: Now to restore ancient institutions fears lack of gradual steps.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring antiquity all at once fears lack of gradual steps.

sentences.zh: 宜先除去聲病偶對之文，使學者得專意經術，以俟朝廷興建學校，然後講求三代所以教育選舉之法，施於天下，則庶幾可以復古矣。”

translations.literal: First remove writing bound to tonal parallelism so scholars may focus on classics, awaiting school establishment—then seek three-dynasty education and selection methods for the realm and perhaps antiquity may be restored.
translations.idiomatic: First remove tonal parallelism so scholars focus on classics, then seek three-dynasty methods and perhaps antiquity may be restored."

sentences.zh: 於是改法，罷詩賦、帖經、墨義，士各占治《易》、《詩》、《書》、《周禮》、《禮記》一經，兼《論語》、《孟子》。

translations.literal: The law was then changed: poetry-rhapsody, fill-in classics, and written interpretation abolished; each scholar mastered one classic among Changes, Odes, Documents, Rites of Zhou, and Record of Rites, plus Analects and Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry-rhapsody, fill-in, and written interpretation were abolished; each scholar mastered one classic plus Analects and Mencius.

sentences.zh: 每試四場，初大經，次兼經，大義凡十道，

translations.literal: Each test had four sessions: first major classic, then supplementary classics, ten great-meaning questions in all,
translations.idiomatic: Four sessions: major classic, supplementary classics, ten great-meaning questions,

sentences.zh: 〈（後改《論語》、《孟子》義各三道。）〉

translations.literal: (Later changed to three Analects and three Mencius interpretation questions each.)
translations.idiomatic: (Later changed to three Analects and three Mencius questions each.)

sentences.zh: 次論一首，次策三道，禮部試即增二道。

translations.literal: then one discourse essay, then three policy questions—the Ministry test added two.
translations.idiomatic: then one discourse and three policy questions—the Ministry added two.

sentences.zh: 中書撰大義式頒行。

translations.literal: The Secretariat drafted great-meaning forms for issuance.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat drafted great-meaning forms for issuance.

sentences.zh: 試義者須通經、有文采乃為中格，不但如明經墨義粗解章句而已。

translations.literal: Interpretation testers had to understand classics and possess literary talent to pass—not merely crude understanding of clauses like Classics Understanding written interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: Testers had to understand classics and write well—not crude clause parsing like old Classics Understanding.

sentences.zh: 取諸科解名十之三，增進士額，京東西、陝西、河北、河東五路之創試進士者，及府、監、他路之舍諸科而為進士者，乃得所增之額以試。

translations.literal: Ten percent of specialized qualifying names were added to jinshi quota; in five circuits newly testing jinshi and in prefectures, directorates, and other circuits converting from specialized categories, the added quota was used.
translations.idiomatic: Ten percent of specialized qualifying names added to jinshi quota; new jinshi circuits and conversions used the added quota.

sentences.zh: 皆別為一號考取，蓋欲優其業，使不至外侵，則常慕向改業也。

translations.literal: All were separately coded and selected—intending to favor their field so they would not encroach outward but constantly aspire to change profession.
translations.idiomatic: Separate codes favored their fields so they would aspire to change profession rather than encroach outward.

sentences.zh: 又立新科明法，試律令、《刑統》，大義、斷桉，所以待諸科之不能業進士者。

translations.literal: A new Law Understanding category tested statutes, Penal Code, great meaning, and case judgment—for specialized candidates unable to pursue jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: New Law Understanding tested statutes, Penal Code, great meaning, and case judgment—for those unable to pursue jinshi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，選人、任子，亦試律令始出官。

translations.literal: Soon selected officials and yin appointees also tested statutes before first office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon selected officials and yin appointees tested statutes before first office.

sentences.zh: 又詔進士自第三人以下試法。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered jinshi from third rank down to test law.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi from third rank down were ordered to test law.

sentences.zh: 或言：“高科任簽判及職官，於習法豈所宜緩。

translations.literal: Some said: "High ranks appointed as secretaries and staff officials—how can law study be relaxed?
translations.idiomatic: Some said: "High ranks become secretaries—how can law study be relaxed?

sentences.zh: 昔試刑法者，世皆指為俗吏，今朝廷推恩既厚，而應者尚少，若高科不試，則人不以為榮。”

translations.literal: Formerly those testing penal law were all called vulgar clerks; now imperial grace is thick yet responders are still few—if high ranks do not test, people will not regard it as honor.
translations.idiomatic: Penal-law testers were called vulgar clerks; grace is thick yet few respond—if high ranks exempt, none will honor it."

sentences.zh: 乃詔悉試。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered all to test.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all to test.

sentences.zh: 帝嚐言：“近世士大夫，多不習法。”

translations.literal: The emperor once said: "Recently scholar-officials mostly do not study law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Recently scholar-officials mostly do not study law."

sentences.zh: 吳充曰：“漢陳寵以法律授徒，常數百人。

translations.literal: Wu Chong said: "Han Chen Chong taught law to hundreds of disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong said: "Han Chen Chong taught law to hundreds of disciples.

sentences.zh: 律學在六學之一，後來縉紳，多恥此學。

translations.literal: Law study was one of the Six Academies; later gentry mostly disdained this study.
translations.idiomatic: Law study was one of the Six Academies; later gentry disdained it.

sentences.zh: 舊明法科徒誦其文，罕通其意，近補官必聚而試之，有以見恤刑之意。”

translations.literal: Old Law Understanding only recited text, rarely grasping meaning; recently appointees must assemble for testing—showing intent to pity punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Old Law Understanding recited text without grasping meaning; recent appointees assemble for testing—showing intent to temper punishments."

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，親試進士，始專以策，定著限以千字。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, the emperor personally examined jinshi, testing policy alone with a fixed thousand-character limit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 3 the emperor personally examined jinshi on policy alone with a thousand-character limit.

sentences.zh: 舊特奏名人試論一道，至是亦製策焉。

translations.literal: Special memorial-name candidates formerly tested one discourse; now they also received policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: Special memorial-name candidates formerly tested one discourse; now they also received policy questions.

sentences.zh: 帝謂執政曰：“對策亦何足以實盡人材，然愈於以詩賦取人爾。”

translations.literal: The emperor told those in power: "Policy response alone cannot fully reveal human talent, yet it surpasses taking men by poetry-rhapsody."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told those in power: "Policy alone cannot fully reveal talent, yet it surpasses poetry-rhapsody."

sentences.zh: 舊制，進士入謝，進謝恩銀百兩，至是罷之。

translations.literal: Under the old system jinshi entering thanksgiving offered one hundred taels of thanksgiving silver; now this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi thanksgiving silver of one hundred taels was abolished.

sentences.zh: 仍賜錢三千，為期集費。

translations.literal: Three thousand cash was granted instead as assembly funds.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand cash was granted instead as assembly funds.

sentences.zh: 諸州舉送、發解、考試、監試官，凡親戚若門客毋試於其州，類其名上之轉運司，與鎖廳者同試，率七人特立一額。

translations.literal: Prefectural recommending, qualifying, examining, and supervising officials—relatives and clients could not test in their prefecture; names were classified and sent to transport commissioners to test with locked-hall candidates—generally one separate quota per seven.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and clients of recommending officials could not test locally; they tested with locked-hall candidates under separate quotas of roughly one per seven.

sentences.zh: 後復令存諸科舊額十之一，以待不能改業者。

translations.literal: Later ten percent of old specialized quotas was retained for those unable to change profession.
translations.idiomatic: Later ten percent of old specialized quotas was retained for those unable to change profession.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，知貢舉蘇軾、孔文仲言：“每一試，進士、諸科及特奏名約八九百人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, chief examiners Su Shi and Kong Wenzhong said: "Each session jinshi, specialized categories, and special memorial-name candidates total about eight or nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yuanyou chief examiners Su Shi and Kong Wenzhong said: "Each session totals about eight or nine hundred jinshi, specialized, and special memorial-name candidates.

sentences.zh: 舊制，禮部已奏名，至禦試而黜者甚多。

translations.literal: Under the old system, after Ministry registration many were dismissed at palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system many were dismissed at palace examination after Ministry registration.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐始盡賜出身，近雜犯亦免黜落，皆非祖宗本意。

translations.literal: From Jiayou all were granted degrees; recently even mixed offenders were exempted from dismissal—neither accorded with founding ancestors' intent.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiayou all received degrees; recently even mixed offenders were exempted—neither accorded with ancestors' intent.

sentences.zh: 進士升甲，本為南省第一人，唱名近下，方特升之，皆出一時聖斷。

translations.literal: Jinshi rank promotion originally honored the southern provincial first place whose announced name was low—specially promoted by momentary imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi rank promotion originally honored provincial first place when announced name was low—by momentary imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 今禮部十人以上，別試、國子、開封解試、武舉第一人，經明行修進士及該特奏而預正奏者，定著於令，遞升一甲。

translations.literal: Now Ministry top ten, separate-examination first place, Directorate and Kaifeng qualifying first, military examination first, Cultivated Classics and Conduct jinshi, and special memorial-name candidates qualifying for regular registration are fixed in regulations for sequential one-rank promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Now fixed regulations promote Ministry top ten, separate-head first, Directorate and Kaifeng qualifying first, military first, Cultivated Classics and Conduct jinshi, and qualifying special memorial-name candidates one rank.

sentences.zh: 則是法在有司，恩不歸於人主，甚無謂也。

translations.literal: Thus law rests with offices and grace does not belong to the ruler—most meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: Thus law rests with offices and grace does not belong to the ruler—meaningless.

sentences.zh: 今特奏者約已及四百五十人，又許例外遞減一舉，則當復增數百人。

translations.literal: Now special memorial-name candidates already reach about four hundred fifty; additionally allowing exceptional reduction of one attempt will add several hundred more.
translations.idiomatic: Special memorial-name candidates already reach about four hundred fifty; exceptional reduction of one attempt will add hundreds more.

sentences.zh: 此曹垂老無他望，布在州縣，惟務黷貨以為歸計。

translations.literal: These men, aging without other hope, spread through prefectures and counties, seeking only corrupt profit as their plan of return.
translations.idiomatic: These aging men spread through prefectures and counties seeking only corrupt profit.

sentences.zh: 前後恩科命官，幾千人矣，何有一人能自奮厲，有聞於時？

translations.literal: Former grace-examination appointments numbered nearly a thousand—has even one exerted himself with reputation in the age?
translations.idiomatic: Former grace-examination appointments numbered nearly a thousand—has even one distinguished himself?

sentences.zh: 而殘民敗官者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Yet those harming people and ruining office are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those harming people and ruining office are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 以此知其無益有損。

translations.literal: From this one knows it is without benefit yet with harm.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows it is without benefit yet with harm.

sentences.zh: 議者不過謂宜廣恩澤，不知吏部以有限之官待無窮之吏，戶部以有限之財祿無用之人，而所至州縣，舉罹其害。

translations.literal: Critics only say grace should be broadened—they do not know the Ministry of Personnel awaits infinite officials with finite posts and the Revenue Bureau pays finite salaries to useless men, while prefectures and counties everywhere suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say broaden grace—they ignore finite posts for infinite officials and suffering prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乃即位之初，有此過舉，謂之恩澤，非臣所識也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of reign there is such excessive action called grace—we do not recognize it.
translations.idiomatic: At reign's start such excess is called grace—we do not recognize it.

sentences.zh: 願斷自聖意，止用前命，仍詔考官量取一二十人，誠有學問，即許出官。

translations.literal: Please decide from sacred intent to use only the prior order; still instruct examiners to select one or two dozen with genuine learning for office.
translations.idiomatic: Please decide from sacred intent to use only the prior order; instruct examiners to select one or two dozen with genuine learning for office.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆補文學、長史之類，不理選限，免使積弊增重不已。”

translations.literal: The rest should fill literary and chief clerk posts without selection limits, avoiding ever-growing accumulated abuse."
translations.idiomatic: The rest should fill literary and chief clerk posts without selection limits, avoiding ever-growing accumulated abuse."

sentences.zh: 遂詔定特奏名考取數，進士入四等以上、諸科入三等以上，通在試者計之，毋得取過全額之半，是後著為令。

translations.literal: An edict then fixed special memorial-name admission numbers—jinshi fourth rank and above, specialized third and above, counted among testers not exceeding half the full quota; thereafter fixed as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict fixed special memorial-name numbers—not exceeding half the full quota; thereafter regulation.

sentences.zh: 時方改更先朝之政，禮部請置《春秋》博士，專為一經。

translations.literal: While reforming prior-court policies, the Ministry of Rites requested a Spring and Autumn Annals doctorate as a separate classic.
translations.idiomatic: While reforming prior policies, the Ministry requested a separate Spring and Autumn doctorate.

sentences.zh: 尚書省請復詩賦，與經義兼行，解經通用先儒傳注及己說。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs requested restoring poetry-rhapsody alongside classic interpretation, interpreting classics by prior commentators and personal explanation.
translations.idiomatic: The Department requested restoring poetry-rhapsody alongside classic interpretation, using prior commentators and personal explanation.

sentences.zh: 又言：“新科明法中者，吏部即注司法，敘名在及第進士之上。

translations.literal: It also said: "For those passing the new Law Understanding category, the Ministry of Personnel immediately assigns judicial posts, ranking above jinshi degree holders.
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "For those passing the new Law Understanding category, the Ministry immediately assigns judicial posts, ranking above jinshi degree holders.

sentences.zh: 舊明法最為下科，然必責之兼經，古者先德後刑之意也。

translations.literal: Old Law Understanding was the lowest category yet required supplementary classics—ancient intent of virtue before punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Old Law Understanding was lowest yet required classics—ancient intent of virtue before punishment.

sentences.zh: 欲加試《論語》大義，仍裁半額，注官依科目次序。”

translations.literal: Wish to add Analects great-meaning test, halve quota, and assign office by category order.
translations.idiomatic: Wish to add Analects great meaning, halve quota, assign by category order."

sentences.zh: 詔近臣集議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered close ministers to assemble for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Close ministers were ordered to discuss.

sentences.zh: 左仆射司馬光曰：“取士之道，當先德行，後文學；

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Sima Guang said: "The path to selecting scholars should first be virtue and conduct, then literary skill;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said: "Select first by virtue and conduct, then literary skill;

sentences.zh: 就文學言之，經術又當先於詞采。

translations.literal: among literary skill, classic learning should precede phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: among literary skill, classics precede phrasing.

sentences.zh: 神宗專用經義、論策取士，此乃復先王令典，百王不易之法。

translations.literal: Shenzong's exclusive use of classic interpretation and policy discourse to select scholars restores former kings' proper canon—the unchanging law of a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong's classic interpretation and policy restore former kings' canon—the unchanging law of kings.

sentences.zh: 但王安石不當以一家私學，今天下學官講解。

translations.literal: But Wang Anshi should not have one family's private learning lectured in schools throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: But Wang Anshi's private learning should not lecture throughout schools.

sentences.zh: 至於律令，皆當官所須，使為士者果能知道義，自與法律冥合；

translations.literal: As for statutes and ordinances, all are what officials need; if scholars truly know the Way they naturally accord with law in secret;
translations.idiomatic: Statutes are what officials need; if scholars know the Way they accord with law naturally;

sentences.zh: 何必置明法一科，習為刻薄，非所以長育人材、敦厚風俗也。”

translations.literal: why establish a Law Understanding category, practicing harshness—not how to nurture talent and enrich custom.
translations.idiomatic: Why establish Law Understanding practicing harshness—not how to nurture talent and enrich custom."

sentences.zh: 四年，乃立經義、詩賦兩科，罷試律義。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Classic Interpretation and Poetry-Rhapsody categories were established; law-interpretation testing abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Classic Interpretation and Poetry-Rhapsody were established; law-interpretation testing abolished.

sentences.zh: 凡詩賦進士，於《易》、《詩》、《書》、《周禮》、《禮記》、《春秋左傳》內聽習一經。

translations.literal: Poetry-rhapsody jinshi studied one classic among Changes, Odes, Documents, Rites of Zhou, Record of Rites, and Zuo Commentary to Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry-rhapsody jinshi studied one classic among Changes, Odes, Documents, Rites of Zhou, Record of Rites, and Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 初試本經義二道，《語》、《孟》義各一道，次試賦及律詩各一首，次論一首，末試子、史、時務策二道。

translations.literal: First session: two original classic interpretation questions, one Analects and one Mencius interpretation each; second session: one rhapsody and one regulated poem; third: one discourse; final: two policy questions on masters, histories, and current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: First session: two classic and one Analects and one Mencius interpretations; second: rhapsody and regulated poem; third: discourse; final: two policy questions.

sentences.zh: 凡專經進士，須習兩經，以《詩》、《禮記》、《周禮》、《左氏春秋》為大經，《書》、《易》、《公羊》、《穀梁》、《儀禮》為中經，《左氏春秋》得兼《公羊》、《穀梁》、《書》，《周禮》得兼《儀禮》或《易》，《禮記》、《詩》並兼《書》，願習二大經者聽，不得偏占兩中經。

translations.literal: Classic-specialist jinshi studied two classics—Odes, Record of Rites, Rites of Zhou, and Zuo Commentary as major classics; Documents, Changes, Gongyang, Guliang, and Ceremonial Rites as middle classics. Zuo Commentary could combine with Gongyang, Guliang, or Documents; Rites of Zhou with Ceremonial Rites or Changes; Record of Rites and Odes both with Documents. Two major classics permitted; two middle classics not both allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Classic specialists studied two classics with major-middle pairing rules; two major permitted, not two middle.

sentences.zh: 初試本經義三道，《論語》義一道，次試本經義三道，《孟子》義一道，次論策，如詩賦科。

translations.literal: First session: three original classic interpretations and one Analects; second: three original and one Mencius; third and fourth: discourse and policy like poetry-rhapsody category.
translations.idiomatic: Classic specialists: three original and one Analects, then three original and one Mencius, then discourse and policy.

sentences.zh: 並以四場通定高下，而取解額中分之，各占其半。

translations.literal: All four sessions together determined rank; qualifying quota halved between them, each half.
translations.idiomatic: All four sessions determined rank; qualifying quota halved between categories.

sentences.zh: 專經者用經義定取舍，兼詩賦者以詩賦為去留，其名次高下，則於策論參之。

translations.literal: Classic specialists decided by classic interpretation; combined poetry-rhapsody by poetry-rhapsody for retention; rank order referenced policy and discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Classic specialists decided by interpretation; combined by poetry-rhapsody; rank referenced policy and discourse.

sentences.zh: 自復詩賦，上多向習，而專經者十無二三，諸路奏以分額各取非均，其後遂通定去留，經義毋過通額三分之一。

translations.literal: After restoring poetry-rhapsody the emperor favored it; classic specialists were only one or two from ten; circuits reported unequal split quotas; later retention was uniformly determined with classic interpretation not exceeding one-third of quota.
translations.idiomatic: After restoring poetry-rhapsody the emperor favored it; classic specialists were scarce; later retention was uniform with classic interpretation capped at one-third.

sentences.zh: 光又請：“立經明行修科，歲委升朝文臣各舉所知，以勉勵天下，使敦士行，以示不專取文學之意。

translations.literal: Guang also requested: "Establish Cultivated Classics and Conduct category; each year ascending literary officials recommend known persons to encourage the realm, promote scholar conduct, and show intent not to take literary skill alone.
translations.idiomatic: Guang also requested: "Establish the Cultivated Classics and Conduct category; yearly recommendations by ascending literary officials to show intent beyond literary skill alone.

sentences.zh: 若所舉人違犯名教及贓私罪，必坐舉主，毋有所赦，則自不敢妄舉。

translations.literal: If recommended persons violate name-teaching or embezzlement, recommenders must be punished without pardon—then they dare not recommend rashly.
translations.idiomatic: If recommended persons violate ethics or embezzle, recommenders punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 而士之居鄉、居家者，立身行己，不敢不謹，惟懼玷缺外聞。

translations.literal: Scholars at home and in districts in establishing self and conduct dare not be careless, fearing stain reaching outside hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars at home dare not be careless, fearing public stain.

sentences.zh: 所謂不言之教，不肅而成，不待學官日訓月察，立賞告訐，而士行自美矣。”

translations.literal: This is teaching without words, accomplishing without severity—without daily school instruction and monthly inspection, rewards and informants—yet scholar conduct beautifies itself."
translations.idiomatic: Teaching without words—scholar conduct beautifies itself without daily school inspection."

sentences.zh: 遂立科，許各舉一人。

translations.literal: The category was then established, permitting one recommendation each.
translations.idiomatic: The category was established, permitting one recommendation each.

sentences.zh: 凡試進士者，及中第唱名日，用以升甲。

translations.literal: For jinshi testers, on the day of passing and name announcement, this was used for rank promotion.
translations.idiomatic: On passing day this was used for jinshi rank promotion.

sentences.zh: 後分路別立額六十一人，州縣保任上之監司，監司考察以聞，無其人則否。

translations.literal: Later sixty-one separate quotas were established by circuit; prefectures and counties guaranteed and reported to circuit commissioners for investigation and memorial—if no person, then no.
translations.idiomatic: Later sixty-one circuit quotas; prefectures guaranteed and commissioners investigated—if no worthy person, none.

sentences.zh: 預薦者不試於州郡，惟試禮部。

translations.literal: Recommended persons did not test in prefectures—only at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended persons tested only at the Ministry, not in prefectures.

sentences.zh: 不中，許用特奏名格赴廷試，後以為常。

translations.literal: If failing, they could use special memorial-name rules for court examination—later becoming regular.
translations.idiomatic: Failure permitted special memorial-name court examination—later regular.

sentences.zh: 既而詔須特命舉乃舉，毋概以科場年上其名。

translations.literal: Soon an edict required special imperial command before recommendation—no blanket listing by examination year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon special imperial command was required before recommendation.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔復通禮科。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Comprehensive Rites category was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Comprehensive Rites was restored.

sentences.zh: 初，開寶中，改鄉貢《開元禮》為《通禮》，熙寧嚐罷，至是始復。

translations.literal: At first in Kaibao, district tribute Kaiyuan Rites was changed to Comprehensive Rites; Xining once abolished it—now restored.
translations.idiomatic: Kaibao changed district Kaiyuan Rites to Comprehensive Rites; Xining abolished it—now restored.

sentences.zh: 凡禮部試，添知舉官為四員，罷差參詳官，而置點檢官二十人，分屬四知舉，使協力通考；

translations.literal: For Ministry tests, chief examiners were increased to four; detailed-review officials abolished and twenty inspection officials established under the four chief examiners for joint comprehensive grading;
translations.idiomatic: Ministry chief examiners increased to four; twenty inspection officials assisted joint grading;

sentences.zh: 諸州點檢官專校雜犯，亦預考試。

translations.literal: prefectural inspection officials exclusively checked mixed offenses and also participated in examination.
translations.idiomatic: prefectural inspectors checked mixed offenses and participated in examination.

sentences.zh: 八年，中書請禦試復用祖宗法，試詩賦、論、策三題。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Secretariat requested palace examination restore ancestral method—testing poetry-rhapsody, discourse, and policy, three topics.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Secretariat requested palace examination restore three topics—poetry-rhapsody, discourse, and policy.

sentences.zh: 且言：“士子多已改習詩賦，太學生員總二千一百餘人，而不兼詩賦者才八十二人。”

translations.literal: It also said: "Candidates mostly changed to poetry-rhapsody; Imperial Academy students totaled over two thousand one hundred yet only eighty-two did not combine poetry-rhapsody."
translations.idiomatic: It said most candidates changed to poetry-rhapsody; of over two thousand one hundred academy students only eighty-two omitted it.

sentences.zh: 於是詔：“來年禦試，習詩賦人復試三題，專經人且令試策。”

translations.literal: An edict then said: "Next year's palace examination—poetry-rhapsody candidates retest three topics; classic specialists for now test policy only."
translations.idiomatic: Next year's palace exam: poetry-rhapsody candidates retest three topics; classic specialists test policy only.

sentences.zh: 自後概試三題。

translations.literal: Afterward all tested three topics.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward all tested three topics.

sentences.zh: 帝既親政，群臣多言元祐所更學校、科舉制度非是，帝念宣仁保佑之功，不許改。

translations.literal: After the emperor personally took power, many ministers said Yuanyou school and examination reforms were wrong; the emperor, mindful of Empress Dowager Xuanren's protecting merit, did not permit change.
translations.idiomatic: After personal rule many said Yuanyou reforms were wrong; mindful of Xuanren's protecting merit, the emperor did not change them.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，議者益多，乃詔進士罷詩賦，專習經義，廷對仍試策。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, critics increased; an edict abolished jinshi poetry-rhapsody for exclusive classic interpretation study; court response still tested policy.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaosheng's start jinshi poetry-rhapsody was abolished for classic interpretation; court response still tested policy.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗念字學廢缺，詔儒臣探討，而王安石乃進其說，學者習焉。

translations.literal: At first Shenzong, mindful of neglected character learning, ordered Confucian officials to investigate; Wang Anshi advanced his doctrine and scholars practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong ordered investigation of neglected character learning; Wang Anshi advanced his doctrine.

sentences.zh: 元祐禁勿用。

translations.literal: Yuanyou forbade use.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou forbade use.

sentences.zh: 至是，除其禁。

translations.literal: Now the prohibition was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the prohibition was removed.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔禮部，凡內外試題悉集以為籍，遇試，頒付考官，以防復出。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites to collect all internal and external examination topics into a register; at each test topics were issued to examiners to prevent repetition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year all examination topics were collected into a register to prevent repetition.

sentences.zh: 罷《春秋》科，凡試，優取二《禮》，兩經許占全額之半，而以其半及他經。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn category abolished; in testing, Two Rites were preferentially taken; two classics permitted half the full quota, the other half other classics.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn abolished; Two Rites preferred; two classics half quota, other half other classics.

sentences.zh: 既而復立《春秋》博士，崇寧又罷之。

translations.literal: Soon Spring and Autumn doctorate was restored; Chongning again abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn doctorate was restored; Chongning again abolished it.

sentences.zh: 徽宗設辟雍於國郊，以待士之升貢者。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong established the Imperial Academy at the suburban altar for scholars advancing by tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong established the Imperial Academy at the suburban altar for tribute-advancing scholars.

sentences.zh: 臨幸，加恩博士弟子有差。

translations.literal: On imperial visits, academy doctors and students received graded favor.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial visits academy doctors and students received graded favor.

sentences.zh: 然州郡猶以科舉取士，不專學校。

translations.literal: Yet prefectures still selected by examination, not exclusively through schools.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prefectures still selected by examination, not exclusively schools.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，遂詔：“天下取士，悉由學校升貢，其州郡發解及試禮部法並罷。”

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, an edict said: "All realm selection shall rise through school tribute; prefectural qualifying and Ministry examination methods are all abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Chongning 3: all selection through school tribute; prefectural qualifying and Ministry methods abolished.

sentences.zh: 自此，歲試上舍，悉差知舉，如禮部試。

translations.literal: From this, annual upper-hall testing was entirely assigned chief examiners like Ministry examination.
translations.idiomatic: Annual upper-hall testing assigned chief examiners like Ministry examination.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔：“大比歲更參用科舉取士一次，其亟以此意使遠士即聞之。”

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict said: "In great comparison years additionally use examination selection once—urgently make distant scholars hear this."
translations.idiomatic: Great comparison years additionally use examination once—urgently inform distant scholars.

sentences.zh: 時州縣悉行三舍法，得免試入學者，多當官子弟，而在學積歲月，累試乃得應格，其貧且老者甚病之，故詔及此，而未遽廢科舉也。

translations.literal: At the time prefectures all practiced three-hall method; those exempted from examination to enter schools were mostly officials' sons, while in-school candidates needed accumulated years and repeated tests to qualify—the poor and old greatly suffered; hence the edict, yet examination was not immediately abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Three-hall method favored officials' sons; poor and old suffered under accumulated years and repeated tests—hence the edict, yet examination was not immediately abolished.

sentences.zh: 大觀四年五月，星變，凡事多所更定。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Daguan, a star changed and many matters were revised.
translations.idiomatic: Daguan 4 fifth month: a star changed and many matters were revised.

sentences.zh: 侍御史毛注言：“養士既有額，而科舉又罷，則不隸學籍者，遂致失職。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Mao Zhu said: "With fixed quotas for nurturing scholars yet examination abolished, those not on school rolls lose their path.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhu said: "With school quotas yet examination abolished, those off school rolls lose their path.

sentences.zh: 天之視聽以民，士，其民之秀者，今失職如此，疑天亦譴怒。

translations.literal: Heaven's seeing and hearing are the people; scholars are the people's elite—such loss of path perhaps draws heaven's reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sees through the people; scholars are their elite—this loss perhaps draws heaven's reproach.

sentences.zh: 願以解額之歸升貢者一二分，不絕科舉，亦應天之一也。”

translations.literal: Please return one or two tenths of qualifying quota to tribute-advancers, not cutting off examination—also responding to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Return one or two tenths of quota to tribute, not cutting examination—responding to heaven."

sentences.zh: 遂詔更行科舉一次。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered examination held once more.
translations.idiomatic: Examination was ordered once more.

sentences.zh: 臣僚言：“場屋之文，專尚偶麗，題雖無兩意，必欲厘而為二，以就對偶；

translations.literal: Ministers said: "Examination-hall writing exclusively favors parallel ornament; though topics have no dual intent, they must be split in two for parallelism;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers said: "Examination writing favors parallel ornament; topics without dual intent are split for parallelism;

sentences.zh: 其超詣理趣者，反指以為澹泊。

translations.literal: those exceeding in reasoning are instead called bland.
translations.idiomatic: those strong in reasoning are called bland.

sentences.zh: 請擇考官而戒飭之，取其有理致而黜其強為對偶者，庶幾稍救文弊。”

translations.literal: Please select examiners and warn them—take those with reasoning and dismiss forced parallelism—perhaps slightly remedying literary abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Select examiners and warn them—reward reasoning, dismiss forced parallelism, perhaps slightly remedying literary abuse."

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，詔罷天下三舍法，開封府及諸路並以科舉取士；

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe, an edict abolished three-hall method throughout the realm; Kaifeng and all circuits again selected by examination;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhe 3 abolished three-hall method; Kaifeng and circuits again selected by examination;

sentences.zh: 惟太學仍存三舍，以甄序課試，遇科舉仍自發解。

translations.literal: only the Imperial Academy retained three halls for graded sequencing and testing; when examination came it still sent qualifying documents.
translations.idiomatic: only the Imperial Academy retained three halls; examination still sent qualifying documents.

sentences.zh: 六年，禮部試進士萬五千人，詔特增百人額，正奏名賜第者八百餘人，因上書獻頌直令赴試者殆百人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Ministry tested fifteen thousand jinshi; an edict specially added one hundred quota places; over eight hundred received regular registration degrees; nearly one hundred who memorialized praise were directly ordered to test.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth year Ministry tested fifteen thousand jinshi; one hundred quota added; over eight hundred degreed; nearly one hundred memorial-praisers ordered to test.

sentences.zh: 有儲宏等隸大閹梁師成為使臣或小史，皆賜之第。

translations.literal: Chu Hong and others, attached to chief eunuch Liang Shicheng as envoys or minor clerks, all received degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Hong and others, attached to eunuch Liang Shicheng as envoys or clerks, all received degrees.

sentences.zh: 梁師成者，於大觀三年嚐中甲科。

translations.literal: Liang Shicheng had himself passed top rank in the third year of Daguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shicheng had himself passed top rank in Daguan 3.

sentences.zh: 自設科以來，南宮試者，無逾此年之盛。

translations.literal: Since establishing categories, southern palace testers never exceeded this year's abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Since categories began, southern palace never exceeded this year's abundance.

sentences.zh: 然雜流閹宦，俱玷選舉，而祖宗之良法蕩然矣。

translations.literal: Yet mixed low-born eunuchs all stained selection—and the good methods of founding ancestors were utterly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yet low-born eunuchs stained selection—and ancestral good methods were lost.

sentences.zh: 凡士不繇科舉若三舍而賜進士第及出身者，其所從得不一。

translations.literal: Generally, scholars not through examination or three halls yet granted jinshi degree or equivalent degree obtained it by diverse paths.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars granted jinshi or equivalent without examination or three halls obtained it by diverse paths.

sentences.zh: 凡遺逸、文學，吏能言事或奏對稱旨，或試法而經律入優，或材武、或童子而皆能文，或邊臣之子以功來奏，其得之雖有當否，大較猶可取也。

translations.literal: Generally recluses, literary talent, officials skilled in speech or memorials pleasing to intent, those excelling in law testing, talent and martial arts, child prodigies all able to write, or border ministers' sons presenting merit—all though right or wrong in obtaining, in broad comparison were still acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Recluses, literary talent, skilled memorialists, law testers, martial prodigies, border sons presenting merit—though uneven, broadly acceptable.

sentences.zh: 崇寧、大觀之後，達官貴胄既多得賜，以上書獻頌而得者，又不勝紀。

translations.literal: After Chongning and Daguan, high officials and nobility mostly received grants; those obtaining through memorial praise were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongning and Daguan high officials mostly received grants; memorial-praisers beyond counting.
